stories.text: Kotak Neo Head of Commodities Research Anindya Banerjee stated that Brent crude prices are expected to remain range-bound with an immediate floor at USD 75–80 per barrel and upside potential extending to USD 115–120. Anindya Banerjee noted that Brent crude is currently trading around USD 91–92 per barrel. Anindya Banerjee stated that the Indian rupee is currently trading around 93.5 against the US dollar in the offshore market and remains undervalued compared to its peers. Anindya Banerjee indicated that the Reserve Bank of India and the US Federal Reserve might each implement one more interest rate hike due to persistent risks from global energy prices. Anindya Banerjee stated that if the situation in West Asia improves, the Indian rupee could appreciate to 91 or 90 against the US dollar over the coming months. Policy makers in India may resist slashing domestic fuel excise duties so public sector oil marketing companies can repair battered balance sheets by holding retail petrol and diesel prices steady. Lauri Myllyvirta, lead analyst at the Centre for Research on Energy and Clean Air, stated that Democratic control of the House will be bearish for oil prices. According to Kpler data cited by Lauri Myllyvirta, India's seaborne oil imports in October were the highest on record for any month.

stories.headline: US stocks: Wall Street ends lower as hot inflation data, Fed comments heighten rate worries
stories.text: US stocks closed lower on Tuesday as a hotter-than-expected inflation reading increased expectations for a Federal Reserve rate hike next month. The US Labor Department reported that the Consumer Price Index increased 0.4 per cent last month, exceeding the 0.3 per cent estimate of Reuters-polled economists. Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller stated that the central bank should raise short-term borrowing costs in December. The S&P 500 lost 29.01 points, or 0.38 per cent, to finish at 7,520.93. The Nasdaq Composite dropped 187.26 points, or 0.74 per cent, ending the session at 25,065.87. Nvidia shares fell 5.4 per cent on Tuesday and have dropped 9.6 per cent over the past two sessions amid an internal probe. CoreWeave shares declined 0.5 per cent during regular trading but rose about 2 per cent in extended trade after beating revenue estimates. The S&P 500 slipped 0.4 per cent on Tuesday after a worse-than-expected inflation report. Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller stated that a stronger policy move may be needed if inflation rose by 0.3 per cent. Nvidia fell 5.5 per cent as the single heaviest weight on the S&P 500.

stories.headline: Consumer inflation rises faster than expected in October, CPI report shows
stories.text: The Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that the consumer price index increased 0.4% on a monthly basis in October. LSEG polled economists who expected the consumer price index to rise 0.3% from the prior month. Core prices were up 0.3% in October, which was slightly higher than the 0.2% estimate of economists polled by LSEG. Energy prices rose 0.7% on a monthly basis in October, while gasoline prices increased 1%. Food prices were up 0.5% from the prior month in October, marking the largest increase for the broader index since April. EY-Parthenon chief economist Gregory Daco stated that inflation surprised to the upside in October with broad-based pressures. Navy Federal Credit Union chief economist Heather Long noted that the implied rate is around 4%, which is well above wage gains of 3.1% in the past year. The U.S. Consumer Price Index increased 0.4 per cent in October after advancing 0.6 per cent in September. Food prices surged 0.5 per cent in October after barely rising in the prior three months. Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller said on Tuesday that the U.S. central bank should raise interest rates next month. Excluding food and energy, the Consumer Price Index increased 0.3 per cent in October.

stories.headline: When is next stock market holiday? Check date for Nov weekday; NSE-BSE closed for Prakash Gurpurab Sri Guru Nanak Dev Ji
stories.text: The Indian stock market will stay closed on Tuesday, 24 November 2026, for Guru Nanak Jayanti. Both the National Stock Exchange and the Bombay Stock Exchange will suspend trading across equity cash, derivatives, securities lending and borrowing, and currency derivatives segments. Normal trading on the National Stock Exchange and the Bombay Stock Exchange will resume on Wednesday, 25 November 2026. Christmas on Friday, 25 December 2026, will be the final scheduled stock market holiday of the year. The Multi Commodity Exchange of India will suspend trading during the morning session from 9 am to 5 pm on the holiday. The National Commodity and Derivatives Exchange will remain closed for the entire day on the holiday. The Nifty 50 rose 0.23% to close at 25,044.65, and the Sensex gained 0.13% to settle at 81,106.65. Equity, currency and debt markets are closed on Tuesday, November 10, because of Diwali-Balipratipada. Trading across equity, currency and debt segments will resume on Wednesday, November 11. The BSE Sensex gained 0.13 per cent to close at 81,106.65 in the previous trading session on Monday. The NSE Nifty 50 advanced 0.23 per cent to close at 25,044.65 on Monday.

stories.headline: US raises 2026 Brent oil price forecast to $97.44 per barrel
stories.text: The U.S. Department of Energy increased its 2026 average price forecast for Brent crude oil by 1.2% to $97.44 per barrel from the previous $96.32 per barrel. The U.S. Energy Information Administration, operating under the Department of Energy, released the report containing the oil price forecast. Global oil prices increased for the third consecutive month in October due to declining global inventories, tanker attacks in the Persian Gulf, limited shipping capacity, and higher transportation costs. Global crude oil prices experienced a decline in the market. Brent crude decreased by 2.2 per cent to trade at 90 US dollars and 51 cents per barrel. West Texas Intermediate crude dropped by 1.8 per cent to trade at 85 US dollars and 27 cents per barrel.

stories.headline: India Sugar Prices: Full Details

sources.name: ABC News & Headlines – Australian Broadcasting Corporation

stories.text: India's Department of Consumer Affairs stated that sugar prices rose by over 30 per cent in August compared to July due to weak monsoon rains straining sugarcane crops. Sugarcane juice seller Dasappa reported that sugarcane now costs him 80 rupees per kilogram compared to 40 rupees previously, leading him to charge 25 rupees for a cup up from about 10 rupees last year. The United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization reported that global sugar prices increased by 6.6 per cent in October, marking the fourth consecutive monthly rise and the highest level since April of last year. India's federal government lifted sugar tariffs to permit duty-free imports of up to 1 million tonnes until the end of the year to increase supply and lower prices before the Hindu festival season. The Karnataka state government is providing about $50 million in support to farmers along with an extra $1.70 for each tonne of sugarcane delivered to mills. Kurubar Shanta Kumar, president of the Karnataka State Sugarcane Growers Association, stated that the crop yield dropped by 9 million tonnes compared to the previous year. Bajaj Hindusthan Sugar, one of India's largest sugar factories, reported a production decline of almost 11 per cent in the last financial year. India is the world's second-largest sugar producer and its biggest consumer. Karnataka's state government is providing about $50 million in financial support to farmers alongside an extra $1.70 per tonne of sugar cane supplied to mills. India's federal government lifted tariffs to allow up to 1 million tonnes of sugar to be imported duty-free until the end of the year and banned sugar from being used for ethanol.

stories.headline: Megaspeed and the battle to get high-end Nvidia chips into China
stories.text: Megaspeed is a Singapore-based data center and AI computing company that manages data center access for Chinese tech firms such as Alibaba. In December 2025, Bloomberg reported that Megaspeed had become the biggest buyer of Nvidia chips in south-east Asia. Megaspeed saw its assets increase sharply from $33 million in 2023 to $3 billion in 2024. Megaspeed has been accused of breaching US export controls to divert Nvidia chips into China, prompting an investigation by US authorities. In December 2025, Megaspeed stated that there was no evidence of any violations concerning the illicit transfer of chips. In December 2025, Nvidia stated that its own inquiry into Megaspeed found no evidence of chips being diverted and no Chinese shareholders. In June 2024, Alibaba lent money to Megaspeed through subsidiaries and remained Megaspeed's largest client. Megaspeed advertises itself as an Nvidia cloud partner providing computing power product services covering Nvidia's entire GPU product line. On December 23, 2025, Megaspeed strenuously denied any wrongdoing in a statement regarding the allegations. The US Commerce Department initially began investigating Megaspeed, but the US Justice Department has since taken over.

stories.headline: Anthropic's new Claude Fable and Mythos models deliver momentum ahead of IPO
stories.text: Anthropic has launched the Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 artificial intelligence models ahead of an expected market debut later this month. Anthropic stated that Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 generate outputs up to 30 percent faster than Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1. Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 are priced at $8 per million input tokens and $40 per million output tokens. In the FrontierSWE v2 benchmark, Claude Fable 5.2 scored 69.9 percent, while Claude Fable 5.1 logged 56.3 percent. In the AutomationBench business workflow benchmark, Google's Gemini 4 Carbon scored 53.9 percent, while Claude Fable 5.2 logged 51.4 percent. In the Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1 benchmark, Mythos 5.2 achieved a score of 74.6 percent. On the RoboDojo benchmark, Claude Fable 5.2 achieved a score of 64.9 percent, compared to OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra at 29.8 percent and Claude Fable 5.1 at 27.6 percent. Anthropic announced the launch of Claude Fable 5.2 and Claude Mythos 5.2 on Monday. Anthropic introduced the two new artificial intelligence models to strengthen its market position amid growing competition. Anthropic is preparing for a planned initial public offering.

stories.headline: Ukraine and Russia discuss prisoner swap deal during ‘constructive’ talks
stories.text: Russian and Ukrainian negotiators met in Abu Dhabi after a nine-month break to discuss ending the four-and-a-half-year war. The two sides discussed a prisoner exchange during the meeting, but an official stated it has not yet been finalized. Tuesday's talks focused on post-war security guarantees for Ukraine and Russia, while Wednesday's discussions addressed the issue of territory. Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy described the talks as constructive and substantive after receiving a report from his negotiating team. According to Russian state media, the talks lasted for 4.5 hours and were conducted in Russian with participation from the United Arab Emirates foreign minister and NATO's top commander in Europe. U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated in Paris that the Abu Dhabi talks appeared very productive while noting significant work remains. Expectations for a breakthrough in the current talks are low because Vladimir Putin shows no sign of wanting to halt the conflict.

stories.headline: Oil hits two-month lows as US eases Iran fears
stories.text: Oil prices fell to a two-month low on Tuesday due to US officials downplaying the need for additional military action against Iran. US West Texas Intermediate crude fell 81 cents, or 0.9%, to settle at US$86.04. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated during a G7 meeting in Paris that US economic sanctions and naval blockade are working. US President Donald Trump stated on Monday that he plans to hold off on new military strikes against Iran. US consumer prices increased by more than expected in October according to US government data. Oil prices fell on Tuesday, Nov 10, to their lowest level in two months due to reduced fears of Middle East supply disruptions. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio stated that economic sanctions and a naval blockade are working, avoiding the need for major combat operations against Iran. US consumer prices rose more than expected in October, leading investors to expect a half percentage point interest rate hike by the US Federal Reserve in December.

stories.headline: Ring cameras go mobile as Amazon debuts AI-powered security drone and robot
stories.text: Amazon announced on November 10 that the Ring Rover Cam and Ring Drone Cam are expected to reach customers at the end of 2026 and in early 2027, respectively. Amazon priced the Ring Drone Cam at $250, matching the starting price of the earlier Ring Always Home Cam. Amazon aims to make the Ring Drone available on January 27, 2027, pending authorization from the Federal Communications Commission. The Ring Drone offers a 148-degree field of view, 360-degree rotation, 2K video resolution, and 8 minutes of flight time under controlled conditions. Amazon priced the Ring Rover Cam at $1,000 for preorder, with shipping scheduled to start on December 16, 2026. The Ring Rover Cam can livestream and record in up to 4K video resolution and cover up to 5,000 square feet. Videos from the new devices will use Ring’s Throw Away the Key Encryption introduced in September 2026, which the Electronic Frontier Foundation stated falls short of end-to-end encryption. Jefferies reports that Indian banks could see margin support from easing crude oil prices and bond yields. Average system liquidity surplus moderated to more than ₹2 trillion in October 2026. Jefferies projects bank credit growth to ease to 14-16 per cent by March 2027.

stories.headline: Alibaba chip unit T-Head files Hong Kong IPO plan amid China’s AI self-sufficiency drive
stories.text: The exchange filing stated that the spin-off and IPO proposal allows for a more efficient deployment of financial resources for Alibaba. The size and structure of the listing have not been finalised yet. T-Head operates as a wholly owned subsidiary of Alibaba that provides full-stack data centre chips to enable system-level compute solutions in China. T-Head is expected to remain a subsidiary of Alibaba after the completion of the proposed spin-off. Alibaba Group announced on Tuesday that its chip unit has confidentially filed a listing application with the Hong Kong Stock Exchange. The Alibaba Group chip unit is named T-Head. The confidential filing with the Hong Kong Stock Exchange followed the receipt of approval to proceed with a spin-off.

stories.headline: Dangote Refinery Gets $4.1 Billion Orders in Top Africa IPO
stories.text: Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals FZE attracted about 5.85 trillion naira, equivalent to $4.1 billion, in share applications for its public offering. Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals FZE initially aimed to raise at least $1.6 billion in the initial public offering. Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals FZE received about $1.9 billion in inquiries from investors in Nigeria and $2.1 billion from international buyers. The Public Investment Corp., overseeing about $220 billion in pensions, requested a large allocation for the initial public offering. Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals FZE is scheduled to submit a draft allotment announcement to Nigeria’s Securities and Exchange Commission this week. Nigeria’s Securities and Exchange Commission is expected to sign off on the share distribution on Nov. 17. Trading of Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals FZE shares is expected to start on Dec. 8, though the company targets the end of the month. Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals FZE is expected to utilize an additional 30% over-allotment option to create room for overseas investors.

stories.headline: Crude oil loses ground on renewed US-Iran deal hopes, but a concrete breakthrough isn't in sight yet
stories.text: Crude oil declined following positive headlines regarding potential progress on a US-Iran deal. Discussions involving Donald Trump, JD Vance, and the Qatari Prime Minister focused on advancing talks with Iran. Donald Trump stated that the United States remains prepared to conduct military strikes against Iran if necessary. The crude oil CFD contract broke below the key 87.00 handle on the daily chart. Sellers are targeting the 80.00 level following the breakdown in crude oil prices. The United States Consumer Price Index report is scheduled for release today. The latest US Jobless Claims figures are scheduled to be released on Thursday. The US Producer Price Index data will be released on Friday to conclude the week.

stories.headline: Oil prices fall to lowest since August as Trump says Iran war is ‘effectively over’
stories.text: Brent crude prices fell nearly 3% to $89.66 on Tuesday morning, reaching the lowest level since August 31. Global markets reacted with relief after Donald Trump stated that the war on Iran is effectively over and downplayed the prospect of further strikes. Europe’s benchmark Stoxx 600 index gained 0.9% to reach 662.54, hovering near an early August record high. Lufthansa shares rose 1.8% and Air France-KLM shares increased by 1.2% as airline stocks climbed on hopes of lower fuel costs. The FTSE 100 index in London climbed 45 points, or 0.4%, to reach 10,828. BP and Shell shares declined by 1.7% and 1.5% respectively, making them the biggest losers on the FTSE 100 index. Daniela Hathorn from Capital.com stated that global markets are extending their recovery following a strong Wall Street session supported by falling oil prices. The AA reported that the average UK petrol price fell by 5p a litre since early October to reach 169.7p a litre.

stories.headline: Gold edges lower as focus shifts to US inflation data
stories.text: Gold prices declined on Tuesday due to profit-taking following a more than 1% rally in the previous session. Spot gold decreased by 0.6% to reach $4,114.48 per ounce at 0430 GMT. US gold futures for December delivery increased by 0.2% to $4,123.50. US President Donald Trump stated on Monday that he intends to delay new military strikes against Iran. Richmond Federal Reserve President Tom Barkin stated on Monday that the US central bank should proceed with care regarding monetary policy. Traders estimate an 84% probability that the US Federal Reserve will raise rates in December based on CME’s FedWatch tool. Spot silver declined by 0.5% to $53.14 per ounce on Tuesday. Platinum remained steady at $1,576.44 and palladium decreased by 0.2% to $1,039.47.

stories.headline: Global gold prices plunge nearly 3% on 10 November 2026 after US inflation exceeds forecasts
stories.text: Global gold prices dropped by nearly 3% on 10 November 2026 due to higher-than-expected US inflation data. Spot gold declined by 2.8% to reach 4,021.36 USD per ounce on 10 November 2026. US gold futures for December delivery dropped by 1.9% to 4,036.00 USD per ounce. Spot silver fell by 3.9% to 51.32 USD per ounce, while palladium decreased by 2.0% to 1,021.22 USD per ounce. The US Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that the headline Consumer Price Index increased by 0.4% last month. Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller stated he would support a stricter policy stance if the CPI report proved excessively hot. The Monetary Authority of Singapore announced the launch of a gold bullion depository service for foreign central banks.

stories.headline: U.S. Inflation Surprises Markets: Gold Plunges 2% as Traders Brace for Steep Rate Hike
stories.text: Gold prices fell more than 2 percent in Tuesday trading following higher-than-expected U.S. inflation data. Spot gold dropped 2.1 percent to $4,051.50 an ounce as of 1427 GMT. U.S. December futures fell 1.34 percent to $4,059.30. The Consumer Price Index rose 0.4 percent last month after a 0.6 percent increase in September, exceeding economists' poll expectation of a 0.3 percent gain. Edward Meir, an analyst at MKS, stated that headline and core CPI came in slightly above expectations and the results were not as good as markets hoped. Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller indicated a willingness to support more aggressive action if inflation came in very high. Spot silver fell 2.9 percent to $51.86 an ounce and palladium dropped 1 percent to $1,031.20.

stories.headline: Gold price update on the morning of November 11, 2026: SJC gold, 9999 DOJI BTMC PNJ Phu Quy rings.
stories.text: On November 11, 2026, the selling price of gold was commonly around 140.9 million VND per tael. On November 11, 2026, international spot gold traded at $4,071.07 per ounce after dropping 1.6%. US December gold futures declined 0.9% to $4,079.80 per ounce. Fed Governor Christopher Waller believes the US central bank should continue raising interest rates in December. According to CME's FedWatch tool, the market priced the probability of a December Fed interest rate hike at approximately 99%. WisdomTree commodity strategist Nitesh Shah stated that if core CPI rises above 0.3%, the market could continue worrying about potential Fed rate hikes. On November 11, 2026, spot silver prices fell 2.1% to $52.27 per ounce, and palladium lost 1.3% to $1,027.97 per ounce.

stories.headline: FCCPC expects petrol prices to fall as crude oil drops
stories.text: The Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission expects a reduction in wholesale petrol costs to reflect in pump prices. Tunji Bello issued a statement in Abuja on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, regarding declining international crude oil prices. Brent crude futures fell from a peak of $115 in September to below $90 per barrel. Petrol sells for between N1,405 and N1,420 per litre in Abuja. Petrol sells for between N1,325 and N1,370 per litre in Lagos. Petrol sold for between N839 and N925 per litre in Lagos and Abuja around the time the conflict began. The Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission will collaborate with the Nigerian Midstream and Downstream Petroleum Regulatory Authority to monitor prices.

stories.headline: Continued U.S. Blockade Of Iran, Not Further Military Strikes, Causes Oil To Dip Below $90 Per Barrel
stories.text: United States president Donald Trump stated on Tuesday that further military action against Iran was unlikely, which caused oil prices to extend their losses and briefly slide below $90 per barrel. Brent crude traded at $90.32 per barrel at mid-session following Donald Trump meeting with Qatari prime minister Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman. West Texas Intermediate traded 2.2 percent lower at $84.77 per barrel on Tuesday. Donald Trump stated on Truth Social that Qatar, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates, Bahrain, and Kuwait prefer maintaining a naval blockade against Iran to prevent the transport of advanced weapons. ING strategists Ewa Manthey and Warren Patterson noted on Tuesday that the market is unwinding geopolitical risk premium expectations as the conflict between the United States and Iran moves toward de-escalation. FGE chairman Fereidun Fesharaki expressed doubt regarding a peace deal, stating that the United States demands all enriched nuclear material to be transferred out of Iran. Global Carbon Project research indicated that global carbon dioxide emissions from fossil fuels are expected to drop by 0.4 percent in 2026 compared to the previous year.

stories.headline: Can Alamos Gold Stock Jump 50%?
stories.text: Alamos Gold shares closed at $55.16 on March 2, 2026, marking their highest close in three years. During the four quarters ended September 2026, Alamos Gold generated $2.28 billion in revenue, representing a 41.5% increase from the previous year. Alamos Gold finished September with $642 million in cash and $227 million in debt. The Island Gold shaft expansion is delayed to mid-2027, which is about one quarter later than previously planned. Management expects the Island Gold shaft to cost 5% more than the initial $835 million budget due to extra ground support needed for rock. Underground mining at Island Gold averaged 1,790 tonnes per day in fiscal Q3 2026, marking a 15% increase compared to fiscal Q2. Alamos Gold management stated that the company remains on track to nearly double its output to approximately one million ounces per year by 2030.

stories.headline: Gold price today: gold falls 2% as hotter US CPI fuels Fed rate hike bets
stories.text: Spot gold prices fell 2% on Tuesday, November 10, trading at $4,054.90 an ounce after the US inflation data release. COMEX gold futures for December delivery dropped 1.3% to $4,060.80 at 13:58 GMT from Monday's settlement of $4,114.50. The US consumer price index rose a seasonally adjusted 0.4% in October, exceeding the Dow Jones consensus of 0.3% according to the Bureau of Labor Statistics. Core CPI rose 0.3% in October, coming in higher than the forecasted 0.2%. Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller stated in London that a 50 basis point hike in the policy rate should be considered if core CPI came in around 0.3 percent or higher. CME Group's FedWatch showed traders fully priced in a quarter-point rate increase at the Federal Reserve's December 8-9 meeting with a 14.7% odds of a half-point move. Silver futures dropped approximately 1.5% to near $51.80 and Bitcoin declined about 2% to near $73,800.

stories.headline: Gold, Silver Fall as Rate-Hike Betting Jumps on Strong Inflation Data
stories.text: Bullion prices fell in volatile London trade on Tuesday as strong United States inflation data increased bets on the Federal Reserve raising interest rates. Market-based odds for the Federal Reserve raising interest rates by 0.25 points in December firmed around 85% after inflation data. The Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that the Consumer Price Index rose 3.7% last month from October 2025. Gold dropped as low as $4033 per troy ounce following the release of the Consumer Price Index data. Silver traded back below $52 per troy ounce, marking an 11-month low hit at the end of October. Crude oil sank 3.5% to push global benchmark Brent to its cheapest level since the end of August. United States President Trump stated that the war on Iran is effectively over.

stories.headline: Brent near $90 offers relief on fiscal, inflation fronts
stories.text: On Tuesday, Brent crude's January contract on the Intercontinental Exchange traded at $90.22 a barrel, marking a 2.54% decrease from its previous close. West Texas Intermediate's December contract on the NYMEX fell by 2.06% to $85.07 a barrel. Pronob Sen stated that the current oil prices are still not comfortable from the perspective of the FY27 budget. In October, under-recovery on domestic liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) was approximately ₹230 per cylinder, while marketing losses for petrol and diesel were ₹9 and ₹12 per litre. India imports roughly 90% of its crude oil requirements, and its crude oil import bill reached about $123 billion in FY26. India's retail inflation rose to a 23-month high of 5.54% in September. According to official data, the Indian economy grew 7.8% in the first quarter of FY27.

stories.headline: How much does it cost to buy silver? Don’t overlook these fees
stories.text: Silver was trading close to $52 an ounce at the beginning of November 2026, according to the article. Steven Rogé explains that a premium is the dealer's price above spot that covers minting, distribution, and the dealer's margin. Henry Yoshida suggests continuing to shop for coins bought mainly for silver if the premium exceeds 20%. Henry Yoshida notes that a spread is the difference between what a dealer sells for and what they will pay to buy it back. Steven Rogé states that one ounce of gold is worth about the same as 80 ounces of silver, but the silver pile costs much more to ship and store. Henry Yoshida states that most dealers list credit card pricing as their standard price and offer discounts for bank wires, ACH, or eChecks. The Silver Institute expects sharp price swings to continue for silver prices, according to the article.

stories.headline: As tech stumbles, is this telecom’s 6.2% dividend yield a safe haven?
stories.text: Verizon Communications shares advanced 9.7% over the past month while high-beta tech names retreated between 15% and 45%. Verizon Communications traded near $45.69 at roughly 11.5 times trailing earnings, offering a 6.2% dividend yield. Verizon Communications reported postpaid phone net additions surged 820% year-over-year to 406,000 in the third quarter. Verizon Communications added 314,000 broadband subscribers in the third quarter and surpassed 1 million net additions year-to-date. Verizon Communications recorded a quarterly free cash flow of $7.8 billion in the third quarter, reaching its highest level since 2020. InvestingPro Fair Value models benchmark Verizon Communications at $54.00 per share, indicating an 18.2% valuation discount. Verizon Communications management raised full-year adjusted EPS growth guidance to between 7.0% and 7.5%.

stories.headline: China crude oil imports hit seven-month high in October
stories.text: China's customs data released on Tuesday showed that October crude oil imports reached 41.94 million tonnes, equating to 9.88 million barrels per day. China's daily crude import rate in October increased by 9.4 per cent compared to September. China's crude oil imports in October decreased by 13.3 per cent compared to the same period a year earlier. Energy Aspects estimated that China's refinery throughput dropped to 13.75 million barrels per day in October. Energy Aspects estimated that China's crude inventories increased by six million barrels in October. China's customs data reported that oil product exports dropped to 5.18 million tonnes in October from 7.16 million tonnes in September. China's natural gas imports grew by 2.4 per cent year-on-year to reach 10.01 million tonnes in October.

stories.headline: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD trades flat around $53 ahead of US inflation data
stories.text: Silver trades flat around $53.00 during the early European trading session on Tuesday ahead of the United States Consumer Price Index data release. United States headline Consumer Price Index is estimated to grow at a faster pace of 3.9% Year-on-Year, higher than the previous 3.7%. The core Consumer Price Index is seen higher at 2.8% Year-on-Year compared to the prior release of 2.6%. On a monthly basis, both headline and core inflation growth remained moderated at 0.3% and 0.2% respectively. The United States Dollar Index holds onto previous day losses near 101.67 as the currency faces pressure ahead of the inflation data. On the daily chart, XAG/USD trades at $53.39 with a bearish near-term bias as the price remains below the 20-day Exponential Moving Average at $54.17. The Relative Strength Index reads at 43 and remains below the midline, indicating that downside pressure persists.

stories.headline: Strait of Hormuz LNG traffic hits highest in October since Iran war began
stories.text: In October 2026, the monthly tally of laden liquefied natural gas tankers exiting the Strait of Hormuz reached its highest level since the U.S.-Iran conflict began. According to S&P Global Energy data, 31 liquefied natural gas tankers passed through the waterway in October, consisting of 23 from Qatar's Ras Laffan and eight from the United Arab Emirates' Das Island. October exports increased compared to the 23 vessels that exited the strait in September. S&P Global Energy senior principal analyst Eric Yep stated that the United Arab Emirates has returned to pre-war transit levels while Qatar is at over 30% of pre-war transits. Kpler shiptracking data indicated that 42 liquefied natural gas cargoes were loaded in October, rising from 27 cargoes in September. Ras Laffan October loadings reached 35 cargoes totaling over 2.7 million tons, marking the highest volume since the war began according to Kpler data. Two vessels carrying liquefied natural gas from Ras Laffan performed ship-to-ship transfers off Oman's Sohar anchorage, involving the SC Prestige, the BW ENN Crystal Sky, the Al Mafyar, Shandong Redwood, and Ejnan.

stories.headline: S’pore opens national currency vault to foreign central banks to store gold reserves
stories.text: The Monetary Authority of Singapore launched a gold vaulting service on Nov 10 for foreign central banks, international financial institutions, and sovereign entities. The Monetary Authority of Singapore national currency vault can currently hold up to 500 tonnes of gold, with expansion room. Deputy Prime Minister and Monetary Authority of Singapore chairman Gan Kim Yong stated that some foreign central banks expressed interest in the vaulting service. Industry testing for the Singapore Exchange over-the-counter gold-clearing system has finished, with live trading expected in the first quarter of 2027. Six banks including DBS Bank, Deutsche Bank, ICBC Standard Bank, JPMorgan, OCBC Bank, and UOB were chosen as clearing members. The Singapore Exchange physically deliverable Gold Kilobar Futures contract is targeted for launch in the second quarter of 2027. The Monetary Authority of Singapore and the Ministry of Finance will introduce an enhanced GST framework effective from April 2027.

stories.headline: Financial institutions eye Asian gold hubs like Singapore: DBS survey
stories.text: Half of the central banks surveyed by DBS Bank stated they are more interested in tapping Asian gold hubs, according to a survey released on Nov 10. Slightly more than half of asset managers and banks expressed similar sentiment in the survey conducted in September by Kantar and released on Nov 10. Only a quarter of central bank respondents in the DBS Bank survey stated they are actively evaluating Asia-based gold hubs for storing official reserves. Singapore announced plans in March to strengthen its status as a gold trading centre by developing capital market products, vaulting standards, and a clearing system. Hong Kong plans to launch a central clearing and settlement system for gold in the first quarter of 2027. Tokenised gold accounts for around 4% of the aggregate gold exposure across surveyed financial institutions. Global gold demand exceeded 5,000 tonnes in 2025, reaching a record US$555 billion in value according to the World Gold Council.

stories.headline: Netherlands says 'difficult' to track product origin, remains among top buyers as India continues Russian oil purchase
stories.text: The Netherlands stated that tracking the origins of petroleum products is difficult, raising questions about European Union sanctions on Russian crude oil. The Netherlands is the third-largest buyer of India's petroleum products and serves as a gateway to the European Union through the port of Rotterdam. India stands as the second-largest buyer of Russian crude exports after China, with Moscow supplying nearly half of India's overall oil imports. India exported $2.78 billion worth of petroleum products to the Netherlands during the April-August period according to the commerce and industry ministry. The Embassy of The Netherlands in New Delhi noted that the European Union prohibits importing petroleum products refined from Russian-origin crude from 21 January 2026. Russian oil supplies reached $33.77 billion, accounting for about 45% of total oil imports totaling $77.56 billion between April and August. Reliance Industries spokesperson stated that the company stopped importing Russian crude oil into its SEZ refinery starting 20 November.

stories.headline: Oil prices, rural stress cloud outlook for consumer goods makers despite volume growth
stories.text: Crude oil prices rose 34% from the end of February to the end of September. Hindustan Unilever Ltd reported underlying volume growth of 7% in the September quarter. Tata Consumer Products Ltd reported 11% volume growth in its domestic business with a consolidated Ebitda margin of 14%. Tata Consumer Products Ltd raised the price of Tata Salt from ₹30 to ₹34 a pack and increased tea prices by 8-10%. Marico Ltd reported a 13% volume increase for Parachute in the September quarter. Britannia Industries Ltd increased prices by 3.5% in the September quarter while palm oil prices rose 17% year-on-year.

stories.headline: API Shows Sharp Build in US Crude Oil, Distillate Inventories
stories.text: The American Petroleum Institute estimated that United States crude oil inventories rose by 9.0 million barrels in the week ending November 6. United States crude oil inventories fell by 5.267 million barrels in the week prior. Total inventory held in the Strategic Petroleum Reserve decreased to 279.5 million barrels for the week ending November 6. On Wednesday at 4:24 pm ET, Brent crude was trading down at $91.96, representing a 0.66% decrease. West Texas Intermediate was trading down by $0.48 per barrel at $86.37 on Wednesday at 4:24 pm ET. United States distillate inventories saw a build of 1.5 million barrels in the reporting period.

stories.headline: Gold, Silver Retreat From Peaks As Bullion Rally Loses Steam
stories.text: Gold and silver prices remained sharply below their MCX contract highs as of the Monday close, with silver down about Rs 1.30 lakh per kg and gold lower by over Rs 34,000 per 10 grams. On 10 November in international markets, spot gold fell 0.4 per cent to USD 4,124.42 per ounce by 0618 GMT following profit-booking after a gain of more than 1 per cent in the prior session. On 10 November in international markets, spot silver declined 0.3 per cent to USD 53.22 per ounce. US gold futures for December delivery rose 0.5 per cent to USD 4,133 per ounce on 10 November. Investors awaited US consumer price inflation data on November 10 and producer price data on November 13 to gauge the Federal Reserve's policy trajectory. The MCX morning trading session was closed on 10 November due to Diwali Balipratipada, with trading scheduled to resume in the evening session.

stories.headline: Brent crude briefly dips below $90 for first time since August on Iran hopes
stories.text: Brent crude temporarily dropped below $90 per barrel on Tuesday, reaching a session low of $89.16 for the first time since August. Brent crude ultimately settled down 1.17% at $91.49 a barrel, while U.S. WTI crude fell 0.93% to settle at $86.04 a barrel. U.S. President Donald Trump stated on Monday that the war with Iran could conclude fairly soon and mentioned that Tehran was speaking very politely. Donald Trump noted following a White House meeting with Qatar's prime minister, Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, that Iran militarily is effectively over. ING strategists Ewa Manthey and Warren Patterson stated that the market is unwinding geopolitical risk premium as expectations of de-escalation grow. Fereidun Fesharaki, chairman of energy consultancy FGE, stated on Tuesday that he sees no prospects of a peace deal between the United States and Iran.

stories.headline: Gold falls nearly 3% as CPI tops forecasts, lifting dollar and yields
stories.text: Gold prices dropped nearly 3% on Tuesday following hotter-than-expected US inflation data that strengthened the dollar and Treasury yields. Spot gold dropped 2.7% to $4,028.39 per ounce by 1:53 p.m. ET on Tuesday. The US Consumer Price Index rose 0.4% last month following a 0.6% increase in September, according to the Labor Department's Bureau of Labor Statistics. The possibility of a 50-basis-point Federal Reserve rate hike in December increased to 10% from 0% prior to the data release, based on CME's FedWatch Tool. The Monetary Authority of Singapore announced plans to launch a vaulting service for foreign central banks and reduce taxes on select gold market companies. Spot silver fell 3.95% to $51.30 per ounce, palladium decreased 1.2% to $1,028.83, and platinum declined 2.7% to $1,534.38.

stories.headline: Gold’s Purchasing Power Against U.S. Real Estate Over Time
stories.text: Since 2000, the price of gold has increased more than 16-fold, outpacing U.S. home price growth according to data from Macrotrends and the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis. In 2000, the median price of a new U.S. home was $167,550, which was equivalent to about 606 ounces of gold priced at $277 per ounce. By the first half of 2026, gold reached $4,514 per ounce and the median new U.S. home price reached approximately $409,600. By 2026, the equivalent of 606 ounces of gold had the buying power of nearly seven homes. U.S. precious metals individual retirement account assets rose from $3 billion in 2005 to $95 billion in 2025, driven by a 38-fold increase in gold individual retirement account assets. Gold's allocation in the optimal World Portfolio rose to 45% in 2025 as investors rethought the traditional 60/40 model.

stories.headline: As Crude Oil Prices Retreat, Sell Soybean Oil Now
stories.text: March soybean oil futures recently hit a six-month low and are trending lower on the daily bar chart. Crude oil prices have retreated from recent highs, creating a bearish factor for soybean oil. The United States has recently harvested a large soybean crop. A drop in March soybean oil futures below last week's low of 62.01 cents would create a selling opportunity. The downside price objective for March soybean oil futures is 55.00 cents or below. Technical resistance for March soybean oil futures is located at 65.00 cents.

stories.headline: When gold has two masters: Demand versus rates and inflation
stories.text: During summer 2026, gold prices experienced competing pressures from hawkish Federal Reserve rate expectations and safe-haven demand driven by persistent inflation and conflict in the Gulf. Stanislav Bernukhov at Exness stated that gold's 260-day volatility rose to roughly 2.1 times that of the S&P 500, marking the highest ratio since 2007. Exness analyst Stanislav Bernukhov noted that gold's 60-day correlation with the S&P 500 index reached approximately 0.70, which is the highest level recorded since 1975. Following a first-half surge above 5,500 USD, Stanislav Bernukhov regards 3,000 USD as a credible medium-term mean-reversion level for gold. Exness analyst Michael Stark expressed the view that gold might gain in the upcoming months because demand remains strong despite the prospect of higher interest rates. Michael Stark mentioned that increasing national gold reserves, specifically in China, are significant over the long term but not practical for his CFD trading timeframes.

stories.headline: Gold ETF vs Crypto ETF: Key differences in India (2026)
stories.text: The Securities and Exchange Board of India has not approved any Bitcoin exchange-traded funds in India as of 2026. Physical gold purchases in India attract a 3 percent Goods and Services Tax along with making charges. Indian residents can invest up to $250,000 per financial year overseas using the Reserve Bank of India Liberalized Remittance Scheme. The first ₹10 lakh of Liberalized Remittance Scheme remittances in a financial year is free of Tax Collected at Source, with a 20 percent rate above that. From 1 April 2026, both gold exchange-traded funds and crypto exchange-traded funds are covered by the Income-tax Act, 2025. Gains on gold exchange-traded funds held for more than 12 months are taxed at 12.5 percent without indexation.

stories.headline: Brent slumps 15% over the past week
stories.text: The front-month ICE Brent contract decreased by $5.95/bbl during the day to trade at $90.59/bbl at 09.00 GMT. Saudi Arabia’s Ministry of Energy verified an attack on the East-West oil pipeline located in the Medina region on 9 November. Kpler head of Middle East and OPEC+ insights Amena Bakr stated that oil price declines mask ongoing threats to Middle Eastern energy infrastructure. Iran rejected transferring enriched uranium out of the country according to state-owned news agency IRNA citing Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei. US President Donald Trump stated in Washington, DC that the US-Israel war with Iran has a good chance of ending soon. Prospects of de-escalation and renewed diplomatic efforts regarding Iran's nuclear programme caused Brent's price to drop around 15% over the past week.

stories.headline: Gold price per tola sheds Rs1,500 in Pakistan
stories.text: On Tuesday, November 10, 2026, gold prices in Pakistan decreased following a weakening international market. The All-Pakistan Gems and Jewellers Sarafa Association reported that the local rate for one tola of gold dropped by Rs1,500 to reach Rs430,836. The price for 10 grams of gold fell by Rs1,286 to settle at Rs369,372. In the preceding session on Monday, gold per tola had increased by Rs3,200 to hit Rs432,336. In the international market, the price of gold decreased by $15 to trade at $4,083 per ounce. Silver prices within Pakistan remained constant at Rs5,723 per tola.

stories.headline: Japan-Vietnam Energy Deals: Why Is Hanoi Turning To Tokyo For Energy Security As Power Demand Surges? $272 Million Funding For O Mon III, Nuclear Power And LNG Projects
stories.text: Vietnamese President and General Secretary of the Communist Party of Vietnam To Lam visited Japan on November 9, 2026, where the two countries signed 11 cooperation documents. Japan and Vietnam signed agreements to fast track energy cooperation in liquefied natural gas, gas-fired power generation, and energy reserves. A financial pledge of about 43.1 billion Japanese yen, equaling roughly $272.7 million, was announced for the development of two projects in Vietnam. The financial pledge includes funding for the construction of the O Mon III thermal power plant project and the Vietnam-Japan University. Japan and Vietnam agreed on a memorandum of understanding on nuclear energy cooperation to facilitate future technology and knowledge sharing. The memorandum of understanding regarding nuclear energy does not represent any concrete decision on constructing and commissioning a nuclear power plant in Vietnam.

stories.headline: Rate Hikes vs Safe Havens: Gold’s 2027–2028 Price Outlook
stories.text: The World Bank lowered its gold outlook, forecasting the metal will average $4,000 per troy ounce in 2028. Goldman Sachs revised its end-of-year gold forecast down to $4,150 from $4,650 previously. Morgan Stanley projected a path to $5,000 per troy ounce for gold in 2027. UBS forecast gold to reach $5,400 per troy ounce by September 2027. HSBC reduced its 2026 average price target for gold from $4,560 to $4,490 and its 2027 forecast from $4,925 to $4,825. Canada’s CIBC cut its year-end gold target to $4,500 from an initial expectation of $6,500.

stories.headline: Asian stocks rise amid falling oil prices on hopes of US-Iran talks
stories.text: Asian stocks advanced on Tuesday following a decrease in oil prices after United States President Donald Trump stated he intends to postpone new military strikes against Iran. Brent crude futures traded down 1 per cent at $91.56 a barrel, hovering at their lowest levels since early September. South Korea's KOSPI increased by over 5 per cent and Japan's Nikkei gained about 3 per cent in early trading sessions. MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares climbed 1.5 per cent, moving away from a seven-month low reached the previous week. Nvidia shares fell 4.2 per cent after the company announced its board was investigating whether CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. Traders are pricing in an 84 per cent probability of a Federal Reserve rate hike next month, according to the CME FedWatch tool.

stories.headline: Red Hill Strikes Exploration Deal with Legacy Minerals for Thomson Gold-Copper Project
stories.text: The agreement allows Red Hill Minerals to earn a 75% project interest after an initial $2 million exploration commitment. Completing the first stage extinguishes Legacy Minerals' right to buy back the net smelter royalty for $6 million. Red Hill Minerals granted Arrow Minerals an exclusive 12-month option to acquire the Pannawonica iron project in Western Australia. Arrow Minerals will provide a $150,000 option fee in shares and pay $1 million in cash or shares if it exercises the option. Red Hill executive chair Joshua Pitt stated that the proposed divestment aligns with the strategy of actively managing the asset portfolio.

stories.headline: Shafaq News..China's crude oil and rare earth imports rise in October
stories.text: China imported 41.938 million tons of crude oil in October, increasing from September, as reported by the General Administration of Customs on Tuesday. Natural gas imports in China fell to 10.013 million tons in October, with cumulative imports reaching 99.215 million tons, according to data. China imported 8,270.2 tons of rare earth elements in October, rising from 6,804.7 tons in September, according to Gelonghui. China's crude oil imports from Iraq rose by 248% in September from August to reach 4.84 million tons, Chinese customs data showed. China's soybean imports dropped to 7.345 million tons in October from 11.88 million tons in September, according to the data.

stories.headline: MSA Drilling Confirms Linked High-grade Polymetallic Breccias - Porphyry Cu-Mo-Au-Ag Centre: Drills 186 m of 0.48% Copper, 0.18 g/t Gold and 10.1 g/t Silver to End of Hole – Company Announcement - FT.com
stories.text: Minsud Resources reported assay results from hole CHDH26-174, which is the first hole of a 10,500 m diamond drilling program at the Chita Valley project located in San Juan Province, Argentina. Drill hole CHDH26-174 intercepted 696 m of continuous sulphide mineralisation from a depth of 50 m to the end of the hole at 746 m. Dr. Renato Bobis, Vice President of Exploration at Minsud Resources, stated that the drill hole confirms continuing high-grade breccias and porphyry mineralisation with geochemistry indicating the system gets hotter with depth. Drill hole CHDH26-174 passed through three stacked mineralised systems, transitioning downwards from a high-sulphidation zone, through an intermediate-sulphidation zone, into a deep high-grade breccia and molybdenum-rich porphyry environment. The Chita Valley Project is owned and managed by MSA, in which Minsud indirectly holds a 49.9% interest and South32 indirectly owns the remaining 50.1% interest.

stories.headline: Arrests made after visit from former US President Biden
stories.text: Former US President Joe Biden visited Trinity College in Dublin on Tuesday accompanied by former first lady Jill Biden. Hunter Biden received the Gold Medal for Outstanding Contribution for Public Discourse at a ceremony during the visit. Pro-Palestinian protesters gathered during the visit to the College Historical Society, and gardaí detained some individuals. At least two arrests occurred after objects were thrown as the family left the venue. The former US president and his family met with Irish Prime Minister Micheál Martin during the trip.

stories.headline: Gold, silver retreat as high core CPI lifts December Fed hike odds- Kitco AM Report
stories.text: The benchmark 10-year U.S. Treasury yield climbed toward 4.94%, and the two-year yield advanced toward 4.69% following the inflation data. Nonfarm payrolls increased by 165,000 in October, and the unemployment rate declined to 4.1% from 4.2%, according to Friday's employment report. President Donald Trump stated Monday that additional U.S. strikes against Iran were not necessary at present after appeals from regional governments. Nymex WTI crude traded near $85.30, and Brent crude traded around $90.50 after briefly falling below $90.00 a barrel on Tuesday. During Monday's U.S. session, the Dow Jones Industrial Average advanced 2.15%, the S&P 500 rose 2.35%, and the Nasdaq Composite climbed 2.74%.

stories.headline: Brent: Iran de-escalation hopes push oil prices lower – Rabobank
stories.text: Brent crude oil prices dropped to their lowest level since September, according to a report by Rabobank’s RaboResearch Global Economics & Markets team. Brent crude oil prices sank by $4.60 to reach $93.70 per barrel over the weekend. The decline in oil prices was driven by trader response to comments from Trump regarding Iran. Trump announced over the weekend that extensive strikes on Iran are highly unlikely if a strong agreement is signed. Rabobank reported that perceptions of winning in the Middle East continue to shift against the backdrop of US Midterm election results.

stories.headline: Oil prices fall as Trump signals pause in military action against Iran
stories.text: Brent crude futures declined 1.7 per cent to $90.99 a barrel on Tuesday, while US West Texas Intermediate futures fell 1.8 per cent to $85.20 a barrel. US President Donald Trump stated on Monday that he plans to delay new military strikes against Iran. Donald Trump stated he will maintain a naval blockade in the Strait of Hormuz for the present time. Opec oil output increased during October, driven by production gains in Saudi Arabia, Kuwait and Iraq according to a Reuters survey. Brent has retreated approximately 22 per cent from a six-month high of $118 reached on October 30.

stories.headline: South32 refinery workers strike as $8b Alcoa takeover looms

sources.name: ABC News & Headlines – Australian Broadcasting Corporation

stories.text: Over 100 workers at South32's Worsley Alumina refinery began a two-day strike for better pay and conditions. The Worsley Alumina refinery is located 200 kilometres south of Perth. Alcoa announced in July a deal worth over $8 billion to acquire South32's bauxite mine and alumina refinery. Unions want a new enterprise bargaining agreement finalised before Alcoa takes ownership in the first half of 2027. Unions claim that South32 employees receive lower pay and work longer hours compared to Alcoa staff.

stories.headline: Gold price hits $4,135, but silver steals the show as Diwali shuts markets
stories.text: December silver on COMEX rose 0.92% to $53.18 a troy ounce around 6:30 am IST on Tuesday, while December gold gained 0.50% to $4,135.20. Indian commodity markets stayed closed for Diwali on Tuesday, leaving domestic traders waiting for the reopening of MCX. Kaynat Chainwala at Kotak Neo stated that democratic gains in the US midterm elections increased expectations of diplomatic efforts with Iran. October nonfarm payrolls rose 165,000, which reinforced expectations of further Federal Reserve tightening. Vikram Subburaj, CEO of Giottus, cautioned that the first MCX print should be treated as provisional due to closed forex markets and incoming US CPI data.

stories.headline: Gas prices dip below $4 but inflation remains stubbornly high
stories.text: The average price of regular gasoline fell below $4 a gallon on Tuesday for the first time in three months, dropping to a national average of $3.98. Consumer prices in October increased by 0.4% from the previous month, according to a report from the Labor Department. GasBuddy petroleum analyst Patrick De Haan forecasts that the national average for gasoline could reach $3.75 a gallon by Thanksgiving. AAA reports that the average price of diesel fuel stands at $6.15 a gallon, marking a decline of about 13 cents over the prior month. Economist Mike Reid of RBC Capital Markets states that higher freight costs are being passed through to heavily imported goods like apparel, recreation goods, and IT equipment. Federal Reserve official Chris Waller indicated on Tuesday that energy shocks might have more enduring effects on inflation, suggesting the central bank may need to raise interest rates more aggressively. The Cleveland Federal Reserve Bank estimated prior to the Tuesday release that consumer prices in October rose 3.7% compared to the previous year. Average wage gains reached 3.1% during the year, according to the data mentioned in the report.

stories.headline: World stocks rise as oil slips below $90 on hopes of US-Iran peace talks
stories.text: Brent crude futures declined by over 2 per cent and fell below the $90 per barrel level on Tuesday due to expectations of potential peace talks between the United States and Iran. US President Donald Trump stated his intention to delay new military strikes against Iran, improving market sentiment ahead of upcoming US inflation figures. The pan-European STOXX 600 index increased by 0.5 per cent, approaching within 1 per cent of its all-time high as declining oil prices mitigated inflation worries. South Korea's KOSPI index rose by 4.4 per cent, Japan's Nikkei index gained 2.9 per cent, and MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares advanced by 2 per cent. Artificial intelligence company Anthropic planned to raise nearly $70 billion through a blockbuster initial public offering, with details briefly circulated to banks. Nvidia shares increased by 2 per cent in premarket trading after falling 4.3 per cent on Monday, while the company's board investigated whether CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence operation. Traders are pricing in an 82.2 per cent probability of a Federal Reserve interest rate hike next month, compared to 74 per cent the previous week, according to the CME FedWatch tool. The United States 2-year note yield increased by 3.3 basis points to reach 4.58 per cent, while the US dollar decreased by 0.1 per cent against the euro.

stories.headline: Trump says Iran war to end 'fairly soon,' plays down prospects of new strikes
stories.text: United States President Donald Trump stated on Monday that the conflict involving Iran could conclude in the near future. Donald Trump declared that the military capability of Iran is effectively finished during a White House meeting on Monday. Donald Trump mentioned that Gulf nations favour maintaining the ongoing naval blockade and Operation Iron Gate against Iran. The ongoing conflict with Iran has persisted for nine months and caused a significant increase in global fuel prices. Iran submitted a two-day proposal to the United States through Qatari mediators demanding the removal of sanctions and a new shipping route in the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian official Mohsen Rezaei disputed claims that discussions with the United States were occurring. United States West Texas Intermediate crude fell over 1 percent to $85.8 per barrel on Tuesday. Brent crude futures declined by more than 1 percent to $91.56 per barrel on Tuesday.

stories.headline: Wall Street slips as inflation stokes Fed hike expectations
stories.text: US consumer prices rose by 0.4% in October, exceeding the 0.3% rise predicted by economists. Federal Reserve governor Chris Waller stated he would support a rate hike in December and noted a firm inflation reading could lead to a 50 basis point increase. The yield on US 10-year treasuries increased by 14 basis points to reach 5.01% at 7am in Auckland. On Wall Street, the S&P 500 declined by 0.8% and the Nasdaq Composite dropped by 1.4%.rices fell. Anthropic announced plans to raise up to US$64.35 billion through an initial public offering by selling 825 million shares at US$70 to US$78 each. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co stated it plans to purchase up to US$500 million of Anthropic shares at the IPO price. Brent crude oil futures decreased by 0.8% to US$91.82 a barrel at 7am.

stories.headline: Federal Reserve Research Reveals New Inflation Threat
stories.text: Federal Reserve economists revealed that oil prices now have a much greater impact on underlying inflation than they did before the pandemic. Fed economists Andrea De Michelis, Musa Orak, Avani Pradhan and Albert Queralto published the findings in a November 9 research note examining five advanced economies. Before the pandemic, a 10-percentage-point rise in relative oil-price inflation increased core inflation by an estimated 0.01 percentage point. After the pandemic, the impact of a 10-percentage-point relative oil-price inflation increase on core inflation grew to 0.14 percentage point. Researchers' model projects that average core inflation across advanced economies could reach approximately 2.8% in the year 2027. Researchers emphasized that their model's projection of 2.8% core inflation in 2027 is an upper-bound scenario instead of an official Federal Reserve forecast. In a simulated 10% oil-price shock, the resulting gross domestic product damage was approximately twice as severe as under pre-pandemic conditions.

stories.headline: Fed Governor Waller sees December hike likely, opens door to possible half-point increase
stories.text: Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller stated on Tuesday that the central bank should proceed with anticipated interest rate increases to protect its credibility. Christopher Waller suggested that a half-percentage-point interest rate increase could be considered for the December meeting. The consumer price index report released on Tuesday showed an October headline price increase of 0.4% and a core increase of 0.3%. Following the October consumer price index report, traders fully priced in a quarter-point rate hike for December alongside 12.5% odds of a half-point move. Dallas Fed President Lorie Logan stated on Tuesday morning that she foresees two additional quarter-point interest rate hikes prior to pausing. The Federal Open Market Committee passed on a rate hike in October through a decision that included dissents from Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack. Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee warned on Monday that the central bank must prevent the economy from running excessively hot.

stories.headline: Midday Need to Know: CPI tops estimates, Treasury yields jump & more
stories.text: The United States Consumer Price Index rose 0.4% month-over-month in October. The 2-year United States Treasury yield jumped 12 basis points to 4.68%. The 10-year United States Treasury yield advanced 5 basis points to 4.93%. The 30-year United States Treasury yield edged up 2 basis points to 5.30%. Shares of Hims & Hers Health tumbled almost 14% after an earnings miss and reduced guidance. Hims & Hers Health stock fell to $19.76, declining $3.18 from its previous close. California voters defeated Proposition 40, which proposed a 5% one-time tax on residents worth over $1 billion.

stories.headline: Fed’s Goolsbee Says AI Data Centers Look Like ‘Old-Fashioned Overheating’
stories.text: Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee stated on November 9, 2026, that the artificial intelligence data center build-out resembles old-fashioned overheating. The two-year Treasury yield finished at 4.56% on November 9, 2026, while futures indicated an 84% probability of a quarter-point December hike by the close. Austan Goolsbee stated that employment and growth are fairly stable while identifying inflation as the Federal Reserve's major problem. The semiconductor index jumped 6.9% on November 9, 2026, after dropping more than 12% the previous week. Richmond Fed President Tom Barkin stated in South Carolina that inflation risks persist and firms are attempting to pass on higher costs. Consumer price index data showed that September CPI rose 0.6% on the month and core CPI rose 0.3%. October CPI data is scheduled for release on November 10, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. ET, with forecasters anticipating a 0.3% monthly rise in headline prices.

stories.headline: Here’s why last year’s government shutdown will haunt October’s inflation data.
stories.text: The overall Consumer Price Index showed prices rose 0.4 percent in October following a 0.6 percent jump in September. Calculations by The New York Times indicated overall prices were roughly 4 percent higher compared with the same period last year, up from 3.7 percent in September. Federal Reserve Governor Christopher J. Waller raised the possibility of a half-point interest rate increase in December if inflation failed to moderate. Two-year Treasury yields increased over 0.1 percentage points on Tuesday to reach 4.67 percent. Average hourly earnings rose 3.1 percent in October compared to a year earlier. Mortgage debt balances increased by $257 billion between July and September to reach a total of $13.4 trillion, according to the Federal Reserve Bank of New York. S&P 500 opened down 0.7 percent and the tech-heavy Nasdaq index declined 1 percent as U.S. stocks began trading in the red.

stories.headline: US CPI preview: Wall Street sees cooler inflation but the Fed may not blink
stories.text: Wall Street consensus estimates headline inflation to rise by 0.3% month-on-month in October, slowing from 0.6% in September. Core inflation is projected by Wall Street to ease to 0.2% month-on-month in October, down from 0.3% in September. Morgan Stanley and Bank of America both forecast an even softer headline inflation reading of 0.2% for October. Fed funds futures price in approximately an 84% probability of a 25 basis point rate hike by the Federal Reserve for December. Bank of America states that only an indisputably soft 0.1% core reading could affect the Federal Reserve's rate hike calculus for December. MUFG targets the EUR/USD exchange rate at 1.12 and the USD/JPY exchange rate at 155 by the end of the year. The Bureau of Labor Statistics will not publish usual annual inflation comparisons due to missing October 2025 data from last year's government shutdown.

stories.headline: UK inflation to overshoot Bank of England target for next 4 years, think-tank forecasts
stories.text: The National Institute of Economic and Social Research stated on Tuesday (Nov 10) that the Bank of England will fail to return inflation to target before 2030. The National Institute of Economic and Social Research forecast that inflation will peak at 4.4 per cent in February 2027. National Institute of Economic and Social Research director David Aikman stated that the United Kingdom economy faces higher energy prices and rising global borrowing costs. The National Institute of Economic and Social Research forecasts that the United Kingdom economy will grow 1.6 per cent in 2026. The National Institute of Economic and Social Research expects the Bank of England to raise interest rates only once, in February. The Bank of England raised interest rates to 4 per cent from 3.75 per cent last week.

stories.headline: Homeowners tap equity as HELOC balances post biggest jump since 2005: New York Fed report
stories.text: Home equity lines of credit balances increased by $23 billion during the third quarter ending Sept. 30, according to a Federal Reserve Bank of New York report. The increase brought total outstanding home equity lines of credit to $481 billion, marking the 18th consecutive quarterly rise according to the Federal Reserve Bank of New York. According to Realtor.com analysis, 49.1% of outstanding mortgages carried rates of 4% or lower in the second quarter. The National Association of Realtors reported that the median price of an existing home was $417,500 in September. Intercontinental Exchange reported that mortgage holders collectively held $17.5 trillion in home equity as of the third quarter. Bankrate reported that the average interest rate for a $30,000 home equity line of credit was 7.49% as of Nov. 4.

stories.headline: Brazil central bank chief says it will keep fighting inflation with tight policy
stories.text: Brazil central bank governor Gabriel Galipolo stated on Tuesday that tight monetary policy will be maintained to control inflation. Gabriel Galipolo spoke at an event in Sao Paulo following minutes interpreted by analysts as dovish. The central bank previously paused an easing cycle last week and held the benchmark Selic rate at 13.75%. President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's spending pledges and reelection contributed to the weakening of the Brazilian real and higher long-term interest rates. Policymakers stated in the minutes that worsening inflation stems from supply-side shocks and that a sharper economic slowdown might limit consumer price spillovers. Gabriel Galipolo affirmed that the central bank will keep raising interest rates when necessary to fight inflation and maintain investor confidence in government securities.

stories.headline: Treasury Yields Turn Higher on Fed’s Waller Comments; Eurozone Bond Yields Fall
stories.text: US Treasury yields increased on Tuesday, with the benchmark 10-year yield surpassing the 5% threshold. The consumer price index increased 0.4% in October, exceeding the Wall Street Journal consensus expectation of a 0.3% rise. Federal Reserve Governor Christopher Waller stated that a December interest rate increase of up to half a percent could be justified if inflation stays hot. The ICE dollar index rose 0.7% to 102.36 as Treasury yields increased. Brent crude oil prices declined 0.6% to trade at $92. The 10-year German Bund yield increased by 0.041 percentage point to settle at 3.307%.

stories.headline: AGFB: Cloud momentum accelerates, but transformation and silver volatility weigh on near-term results
stories.text: Agfa-Gevaert NV reported flat continuing Q3 sales alongside an adjusted EBITDA decline to EUR 1 million. The weak financial performance was driven by poor Imaging & Advanced Materials results and silver-related volatility. HealthCare IT cloud orders experienced a surge despite the transition weighing on near-term profitability. Agfa-Gevaert NV expects margin inflection to occur in the year 2028.

stories.headline: Indonesia's Antam Gold Price Rises Rp15,000; Buyback Jumps Rp25,000 per Gram
stories.text: PT Aneka Tambang Tbk gold selling price for 1-gram increased by Rp15,000 to reach Rp2.56 million in Tuesday trading on 11/10/2026. The buyback price for PT Aneka Tambang Tbk gold jumped by Rp25,000 to reach Rp2.375 million per gram. Purchases of PT Aneka Tambang Tbk gold bars are subject to an Article 22 Income Tax of 0.25% for taxpayers holding a tax identification number. Galeri24 gold was recorded at a price of Rp2.518 million per gram with a buyback price of Rp2.37 million per gram.

stories.headline: West Africa’s gold boom puts spotlight on geology, data quality and responsible mining
stories.text: Ivan Doku stated that current exploration programmes in countries like Ghana and Côte d’Ivoire are utilizing a combination of drilling, soil sampling, and geophysical surveys. Roanne Sutcliffe of SRK Consulting (South Africa) noted that international mining houses are selling assets to local companies or consortia, reflecting evolving ownership structures. Ivan Doku explained that mineralisation in West Africa’s structurally controlled gold deposits may occur in narrow veins featuring associated structural complexities. Ivan Doku noted that in parts of Ghana’s Ashanti Belt, mineralisation has stayed difficult to exploit because existing processing technology has failed to deliver adequate recovery.

stories.headline: Zijin Mining stock: Gold Mountains sees lasting metals demand
stories.text: Gold Mountains Asset Management reported a durable investment case for gold, copper and uranium on Tuesday, November 10. Gold Mountains Asset Management managing director Lisa Liu stated that gold producers are generating strong net cash flow. Gold Mountains Asset Management completed its first streaming deal in 2024 and plans to pursue more royalty and streaming transactions. Lisa Liu highlighted uranium due to rising power demand in Europe, North America and China.

stories.headline: Gold and silver prices rise after Diwali: Gold rises ₹968 to ₹1.42 lakh; silver becomes ₹3,132 costlier, se...
stories.text: According to the India Bullion and Jewellers Association, the price of 10 grams of 24-carat gold increased by ₹968 to ₹1.42 lakh after Diwali. The price of 1 kilogram of silver rose by ₹3,132 to reach ₹1.86 lakh. Prior to Diwali on Dhanteras, gold prices had fallen by ₹2,677 to around ₹1.41 lakh. On Dhanteras before Diwali, one kilogram of silver became ₹4,432 cheaper and fell to ₹1.83 lakh.

stories.headline: Africa Emerges as a New Global Growth Hub for LNG
stories.text: The African Energy Chamber forecasts that Africa's upstream oil and gas sector will attract approximately $40 billion in annual investment by 2030, with daily production reaching 12.5 million barrels of oil equivalent. Eni has invested $7.2 billion in the Coral North floating LNG project in Mozambique and commenced offshore drilling with a target production start date of 2028. The Nigeria LNG Train 7 expansion project is set to come online in 2027, increasing Nigeria's total LNG production capacity to 30 mtpa. The Greater Tortue Ahmeyim project, shared by Senegal and Mauritania, exported its first cargo of LNG in April 2025 with an initial capacity of 2.5 mtpa.

stories.headline: US-Iran deal hopes weigh on WTI as it trades below $85
stories.text: West Texas Intermediate futures on NYMEX traded just below $85.00, down 1.5% during Tuesday’s Asian session and near Monday’s 10-week low of $84.25. Growing optimism over a potential agreement between the United States and Iran is weighing heavily on oil prices, according to analysts at MUFG. Trading at $84.81 on the daily chart, West Texas Intermediate US Oil retains a bearish near-term bias well below the 20-day Exponential Moving Average of $93.36. The Relative Strength Index for West Texas Intermediate sits at 34, just above oversold territory, indicating that downward momentum remains intact.

stories.headline: Two-year U.S. Treasury yield posts biggest one-day rise since 2024
stories.text: The two-year U.S. Treasury yield experienced its largest single-day surge since 2024 following the October inflation report released on Tuesday. Bond traders priced in steeper Federal Reserve interest rate hikes in response to the October Consumer Price Index release. Inflation pressures strengthened beyond the average economist estimate in the October Consumer Price Index release. The odds of a 50-basis-point Federal Reserve interest rate hike jumped to 14.7% after previously sitting at zero. A 25-basis-point interest rate hike remains the dominant market expectation at 85.3%.

stories.headline: US inflation rose 0.4% in October as price increases cooled and gas costs dipped
stories.text: US inflation rose 0.4% from September to October, according to data from the Bureau of Labor Statistics. Oxford Economics estimated that the topline inflation figure for October 2026 would have been 3.9%. Energy prices rose 0.7% in October after increasing 5.2% in September. The US Federal Reserve raised interest rates in September for the first time since 2023. Federal Reserve chair Kevin Warsh stated on 28 October that the central bank is dedicated to ensuring price increases ease up.

stories.headline: Higher US yields could push India towards export-led growth: SBICAPS
stories.text: SBICAPS stated that India's traditional advantage of providing significantly higher returns than developed markets is shrinking, making it more difficult to attract foreign capital to finance current account deficits. The SBICAPS report indicates that India possesses relatively stable economic fundamentals backed by anchored inflation, gradual fiscal consolidation, and an improving sovereign credit profile. SBICAPS noted that about 75-85 per cent of the increase in US yields since 2020 has been caused by inflation and aggressive monetary tightening. SBICAPS stated that the United States economy's natural rate of interest is being driven up by persistent government borrowing, increased Treasury issuance, productivity gains from artificial intelligence, and diversification away from dollar assets. SBICAPS highlighted that India's inflation premium over the United States has narrowed over the past decade, resulting in compressed yield spreads between the two countries.

stories.headline: USD/INR Closes at 93.93 as Dollar Buying Halts Rupee Rally
stories.text: The USD/INR exchange rate closed at 93.9275 on 9 November 2026, marking a daily increase of 0.024% and ending a six-session winning streak for the Indian rupee. State-run Indian banks purchased US dollars during the 9 November session, causing the exchange rate to rebound 23.75 paise from an intraday low of 93.69. Brent crude settled at $92.57 per barrel on 9 November 2026, down $5.75 or 5.85%, following comments that reduced expectations of renewed military strikes on Iran. Foreign institutional investors purchased a provisional net ₹7,212.22 crore in Indian equities on 9 November 2026. Indian domestic currency markets are closed on 10 November 2026 for Diwali-Balipratipada and are scheduled to reopen on Wednesday, 11 November 2026.

stories.headline: Reuters Survey: OPEC Production Rose in October to 90% of Pre-War Levels
stories.text: A Reuters survey revealed an increase in oil production by the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries in October. The rise in oil production was driven by higher output from Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, and Iraq. Total crude oil production reached 22.87 million barrels per day in October.

stories.headline: Weekly Rupee View: Poised for further gains
stories.text: The rupee appreciated by 81 paise against the dollar over the past week and closed at 93.94 on Monday. Net FPI inflows so far in November stand at around $6.4 billion according to NSDL data. The rupee closed above the key resistance at 94.20, breaking out of the broad 94.20-96.80 range.

stories.headline: Why Did Brent Oil Fall Faster Than WTI During the Iran Negotiations?
stories.text: Brent crude fell faster than West Texas Intermediate on November 9, 2026, settling 5.85% lower at $92.57 a barrel, while West Texas Intermediate dropped 4.38% to $86.85. President Donald Trump decided to defer fresh military strikes on Iran, easing escalation concerns and reducing fears of disruption to Gulf oil exports. JPMorgan estimated that the global oil market experienced a surplus of 1.1 million barrels per day in September, which widened to 1.4 million barrels per day in October.

stories.headline: Thirsty farms, slowing turbines: how depleting dams threaten power, harvest
stories.text: Water levels at India's 178 reservoirs dropped 27% from a year ago to 121.9 billion cubic metres due to scanty monsoon rains. The Reserve Bank of India warned about mounting risks to food inflation driven by the ongoing dry spell. Sowing across India dropped to 11.7 million hectares till 6 November compared to 14.1 million hectares during the same period last year. Agriculture ministry data showed wheat acreage slipped 12% to 1.97 million hectares, rice dropped 3.10% to 673,000 hectares, and pulses fell 14.4% to 3.2 million hectares. The World Meteorological Organization warned in September that the 2026 El Niño could push Pacific Ocean temperatures 3.8°C above average. India's southwest monsoon rainfall in 2026 reached 87% of the 50-year average, registering as the fourth-lowest since 2001. Maharashtra expanded drought relief in late October to 305 of the state's 358 talukas, approving a ₹ 7,500-crore package. India witnessed a record power demand of 270.8GW in May this year, according to the report.

stories.headline: Vale Stocks Fall 3.84% as China Pollution Curbs Weigh on Iron Ore
stories.text: Vale shares dropped 3.84% to $11.51 during regular trading on November 10, reversing a previous gain. The decline in Vale stock followed emergency pollution curbs implemented in Chinese steelmaking hubs Tangshan and Handan. Dalian's most-traded contract decreased 0.73% to 684.5 yuan a ton, and Singapore's December contract dropped 0.58% to $92.5.
