Chinese hot metal output decreased for a fourth consecutive week to 2.31 million tons a day, marking its lowest level since late March. During the third quarter, Brazilian miner Vale reported an adjusted EBITDA decline of 24% to $3.33 billion. Vale reported a net income drop of 53% to $1.26 billion for the third quarter. The Chief Financial Officer of Vale has stated that there will be no extraordinary dividend distributed this year. GuruFocus assigns Vale a score of 76/100 and considers the shares fairly valued at $12.55.

stories.headline: Mauritius-based investment firm Soach Global founder moots demat holding of foodgrains
stories.text: Anubhav Dayal, founder and director of Soach Global Opportunities Fund, proposed a virtual food grain asset concept at a Securities and Exchange Board of India Ideathon. Anubhav Dayal stated that the virtual food grain asset proposal is currently at a concept stage and needs compliance with existing regulations. Depositories would hold virtual food grain assets in dematerialised form to facilitate trading on exchanges before turning physical upon maturity. Groups such as cooperative societies or farmer producing companies would issue virtual food grain assets into the demat accounts of farmers. Village panchayats would endorse forecasted production for each farmer, allowing the cooperative society to issue corresponding certificates. Anubhav Dayal noted that settlement for virtual food grain assets differs from cash-settled options because it requires physical delivery of the produce. Initial focus for the crops covered would be placed on those for which the government has fixed the minimum support price. Anubhav Dayal stated that the next step for the Soach Global Opportunities Fund founder is preparing a detailed report for Securities and Exchange Board of India review.

stories.headline: India engaging with Moscow, Kyiv on Black Sea shipping safety, grain, energy exports: MEA
stories.text: India is engaging with Russia and Ukraine regarding proposals to de-escalate the conflict, secure Black Sea shipping, and facilitate grain and energy exports, according to the Ministry of External Affairs on Tuesday. Trilateral talks involving Russia, Ukraine, and the United States commenced in the United Arab Emirates to explore a peaceful resolution to the conflict. External Affairs Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal stated that India has consistently advocated dialogue and diplomacy, with Prime Minister Narendra Modi urging an end to the war. Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy held a phone conversation on Monday to discuss the ongoing war and humanitarian consequences. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that Ukraine is counting on India's willingness to mediate in establishing food corridors and addressing Russia's blockade of Black Sea grain exports. External Minister S Jaishankar spoke with Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov regarding ongoing diplomatic efforts to end the conflict, as stated by the Ministry of External Affairs. Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha stated about a month ago that Kyiv received separate ceasefire proposals from India and three other countries. Russian President Vladimir Putin stated last month that Prime Minister Narendra Modi had presented good ideas for finding a mutually acceptable solution to the conflict.

stories.headline: DiDi seeks to expand electric vehicle use beyond China
stories.text: In 2025, fully electric vehicles accounted for 74% of the kilometers traveled on rides booked through DiDi in China, according to the company. Stephen Zhu stated that replacing combustion-engine vehicles with electric models cuts operating costs by 30% to 60%. DiDi has more than 100,000 electric and hybrid vehicles registered on its platform in Brazil, compared to just over 10,000 in Mexico. DiDi's financial arm, 99Pay, has more than 28 million accounts and has extended R$9 billion in credit since 2018, according to Simeng Wang. At the end of September, DiDi Volt operated more than 80,000 stations and nearly 350,000 fast-charging connectors across more than 300 cities in China. According to the Brazilian Electric Vehicle Association, electric and hybrid models represented 21.5% of light vehicle sales in October in Brazil, totaling 54,486 units. Brazil recorded 29,866 charging stations in September, which included 11,397 fast-charging points, according to a survey by the ABVE and Tupi Mobilidade. The National Energy Policy Council established a working group on Friday (6) to formulate a National Electromobility Strategy within 120 days.

stories.headline: Nvidia’s value tumbles after ‘honeytrap’ investigation launched, as China denies spying claims – as it happened
stories.text: Nvidia shares declined by 5% on Monday following reports that CEO Jensen Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort. Nvidia announced on Sunday that it opened an investigation after Jensen Huang admitted to having an affair with Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based datacenter company Megaspeed. US intelligence determined that Alice Huang was gathering information for China, according to the New York Times. US President Donald Trump downplayed the revelations about Jensen Huang on Sunday, stating he believes Huang is a fine person and should stay on as CEO. A US commerce department investigation into Megaspeed was halted after Nvidia general counsel Tim Teter intervened and contacted investigators. US Republican lawmakers asked Jensen Huang to provide a closed-door briefing next week to the House foreign affairs and intelligence committees. Nvidia's board stated on Sunday that it has no reason to believe US national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised. Briefing.com analyst Patrick O’Hare noted that investors are treating Nvidia as a one-off story rather than anticipating a systemic domino effect.

stories.headline: ‘Everything and everyone we love is at stake’: Thunberg slams COP31 talks
stories.text: Swedish climate activist Greta Thunberg criticized the United Nations climate talks as hypocritical on Tuesday during her arrival at the COP31 conference. Greta Thunberg stated that negotiations are filled with lobbyists paid by destructive industries benefiting from the current status quo. The COP31 talks follow a year of deadly climate-related disasters and an energy shock caused by the US-Israel war on Iran. COP31 co-hosts Turkiye and Australia promote renewable energy and rooftop solar installations while still relying heavily on fossil fuels. The Antalya summit marks the first COP conference Greta Thunberg has attended since the 2021 talks held in Glasgow, Scotland. COP31 is taking place in the Turkish resort city of Antalya and runs until November 20. Next year’s COP32 climate conference is scheduled to be held in Ethiopia’s capital, Addis Ababa, in November 2027.

stories.headline: Nvidia hires major US law firm to investigate alleged Chinese spy affair
stories.text: Nvidia hired the US law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to investigate the romantic relationship between Chief Executive Jensen Huang and an alleged Chinese spy named Alice Huang. Attorney Joon Kim will lead the independent investigation for Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz, while the Federal Bureau of Investigation conducts a separate probe. Nvidia has experienced a stock market value drop of $500 billion, with £375 billion wiped off since Friday, pushing the share price almost to a yearly low. Alice Huang was an executive at Megaspeed, a Singaporean company and Nvidia customer that was suspected of helping divert Nvidia chips to China. US President Donald Trump stated on Monday that he spoke with Jensen Huang, who claimed he had no idea Alice Huang was a spy. Congressional leaders of the House Committee on Foreign Affairs requested Jensen Huang to appear next week for a closed-door briefing. Nvidia's board announced on Sunday that a committee of independent directors would oversee the probe and stated they had no reason to believe company secrets or national security were compromised.

stories.headline: Chashma 5 Nuclear Power Plant in Pakistan Reaches Major Milestone in China-Backed Construction
stories.text: The Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission completed the installation of the reactor building dome at the Chashma 5 nuclear plant site in Mianwali, Punjab, on November 10, 2026. The Chashma 5 nuclear project is targeted to begin electricity generation in September 2030. Once operational, the Chashma 5 unit will add 1,200MW of gross generating capacity to the electricity system of Pakistan. Pakistan approved the Chashma 5 project in 2023 at a revised cost of approximately PKR 1.048 trillion, equating to US$3.7 billion. The Pakistan Nuclear Regulatory Authority issued the Chashma 5 construction licence on December 26, 2024. The Chashma 5 nuclear plant will use China’s Hualong One reactor design, also referred to as HPR1000. The Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission is developing the project in partnership with the China Zhongyuan Engineering Corporation.

stories.headline: France awards $1.7 billion contract to Airbus-Thales team for new military satellites
stories.text: France’s Directorate General of Armament awarded a contract worth €1.5 billion, or $1.7 billion, to Airbus Defence and Space and Thales Alenia Space. The contract is meant to procure two high-resolution Earth-observation satellites for the French armed forces under the IRIS military satellite program. Alain Fauré, head of Space Systems at Airbus Defence and Space, stated that the program strengthens the French supply chain in space-based optical imagery. The new IRIS orbiters are intended to replace three existing Optical Space Component satellites currently in use. The Directorate General of Armament stated that the new satellites are expected to be in orbit by 2035, with the first becoming operational by 2033. Airbus will act as the lead contractor to supply both satellite platforms, most of the first satellite’s payload, and oversee the ground segment. Thales Alenia Space will act as a co-contractor to provide the optical systems for the IRIS program.

stories.headline: Violence erupts in Bangladesh as ousted PM's supporters stage protest
stories.text: Police in Bangladesh fired tear gas and rubber bullets against supporters of ousted Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina who demanded her return. A 60-year-old bus driver died from smoke inhalation after a vehicle was set on fire in Faridpur on Tuesday. About 200 protesters briefly blocked traffic on the 6.2km Padma bridge across the Ganges connecting Dhaka to the south-western region. Bangladesh Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed stated that any attempts to create instability from across the border in India will not succeed. The United Nations estimated that up to 1,400 people were killed, mostly by security forces gunfire, during anti-government protests in 2024. Sheikh Hasina requested a passport from the Bangladesh High Commission in New Delhi after stating in December she wanted to return. Bangladesh junior foreign affairs minister Humaiun Kobir stated that the government would not provide a passport and called Sheikh Hasina a terrorist.

stories.headline: Portugal slams Rutte for ‘regrettable’ claim that Lisbon downplays Russian threat
stories.text: Portugal's foreign ministry criticized NATO chief Mark Rutte on Tuesday for claiming Lisbon views the Russian threat as distant and less relevant. Mark Rutte stated on Dutch TV last week that Southern European nations like Spain and Portugal view Russian aggression as remote. Mark Rutte remarked that Russia's newest missiles take just five minutes longer to reach Lisbon than they do Warsaw. NATO spokesperson Allison Hart stated that all allies agree Russia is a threat. Spain has provided 1.5 billion euros in military and humanitarian aid to Ukraine since 2022, representing 0.2 percent of its GDP, based on Kiel Institute data. Portugal has contributed 390 million euros, or 0.18 percent of its GDP, in aid to Ukraine. A Eurobarometer poll from this spring showed that 92 percent of surveyed individuals in Portugal viewed the Russian invasion as a security threat to the European Union.

stories.headline: Philip R. Lane: The science and practice of monetary policy communication: the ECB experience
stories.text: Philip R. Lane stated that monetary policy communication steers financial market participants' expectations and shapes financing conditions across maturity and risk spectrums. Large language models and machine learning techniques allow automated analysis of large volumes of text by evaluating the context in which words are used. European Central Bank research shows that internal measures of communication tone track shifts in the deposit facility rate, turning hawkish during tightening and dovish during easing. Research from the European Central Bank indicates that information extracted from monetary policy statements improves forecasts of euro area core inflation several quarters ahead. Data presented from the European Central Bank's 2021 monetary policy strategy review indicates that information regarding the new inflation target reached approximately one in ten consumers following its announcement. European Central Bank research demonstrates that unexpected shifts in monetary policy communication generally have smaller and slower macroeconomic effects than unexpected interest rate decisions. European Central Bank meeting day monetary policy surprises can be partially inferred from euro area equity market movements over the preceding six weeks.

stories.headline: Mutual funds' Nifty 50 allocation falls to 21-year low in Q2
stories.text: Domestic mutual funds allocated 49.4 per cent to Nifty 50 stocks in the September quarter, dropping below 50 per cent for the first time in 21 years. Scripbox Founder and CEO Atul Singhal stated that foreign investors withdrew about $65 billion over two years, primarily from large caps. The Nifty 50 achieved annualised returns of 4.8 per cent over the three years ending in September. The Nifty Midcap 150 generated annualised returns of 13 per cent over the three-year period ending September. Small-cap funds pulled in ₹9,039 crore and mid-cap schemes attracted ₹7,835 crore in September according to the Association of Mutual Funds in India. Mutual funds' ownership in Nifty 50 companies' market capitalisation climbed to a record 14.8 per cent in September. Overall institutional allocation to Nifty 50 stocks dropped to a record low of 54.6 per cent.

stories.headline: Piero Cipollone: Cash and the digital euro: two sides of the same coin
stories.text: Piero Cipollone stated that the Parliament adopted its position on the Single Currency Package on 9 July. On 2 November, the Pontes platform settled the issuance of the European Stability Mechanism's first digitally native benchmark bond worth €1 billion. Piero Cipollone stated that the digital euro pilot will start in the second half of 2027. In July, the European Central Bank announced the 36 payment service providers selected for the pilot from more than 50 applicants. Piero Cipollone stated that the innovation work on the digital euro platform, including testing conditional payments and artificial intelligence, will run from January to June 2027. Piero Cipollone reported that a survey on new euro banknote designs received almost 10 million responses. Piero Cipollone stated that the first denominations of the new banknote series are expected to enter circulation in the early 2030s.

stories.headline: Japan's Proposed USD-500 Billion Defence Expansion
stories.text: Japan is considering a defence spending allocation of US$457-508 billion over five years starting from April 2027. Japan's FY2026 defence-related budget totals approximately US$60.2 billion, which includes US$58.7 billion in programme expenditure. Japan's SHIELD unmanned coastal defence initiative received approximately US$0.667 billion in FY2026 funding. Japan's FY2026 funding includes approximately US$1.07 billion for fighter development and engine design under the GCAP programme. Japan revised its defence equipment transfer principles and implementation guidelines on April 21, 2026. Mitsubishi Heavy Industries reported FY2025 Aircraft, Defence & Space segment revenue of approximately US$12.9 billion. Kawasaki Heavy Industries generated approximately US$4.1 billion from its Aerospace Systems segment in FY2025.

stories.headline: France blames Iran for fridge attacks
stories.text: France stated that Iran was responsible for cyberattacks that hacked and overheated supermarket refrigerators in October Hackers exploited a known flaw in internet-connected industrial refrigeration systems across hundreds of supermarkets in France French prosecutors attributed the October attacks to the Shahid Kaveh cyber crime group linked to Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corp Paris public prosecutor Laure Beccuau stated that the attackers used Farsi and IP addresses traced back to devices in Iran The Paris Public Prosecutor's Office is investigating the incident and has issued international warrants against members of Shahid Kaveh Jean-Noël Barrot, the French minister for Europe and Foreign Affairs, called for Europe-wide sanctions against Iran at the G7 summit in Paris The French campaign impacted approximately 700 commercial sites while a second wave affected over 100 establishments across Europe

stories.headline: JLR identifies India as key growth market, to launch first EV in 2027: MD
stories.text: Jaguar Land Rover identified India as a key growth market and plans to launch its first electric vehicles in the country in 2027. Jaguar Land Rover India Managing Director and CEO Rajan Amba stated that the company will introduce the new Jaguar GT next year. Jaguar Land Rover plans to initially import its electric models to test market response in India. Jaguar Land Rover expects to increase its retail outlets in India to 40 by the end of this year from 25 a year ago. Jaguar Land Rover witnessed a surge in demand following price reductions on certain models due to the India-UK free trade agreement. Rajan Amba cited an example of a vehicle whose price dropped from around Rs 4.25 crore to Rs 3.5 crore following price revisions. Jaguar Land Rover expects around 20 per cent growth in orders for the Defender brand due to localisation.

stories.headline: Moats Under Siege: Europe’s Energy Transition and Future Threats from China & USA
stories.text: Unwinding a failed project in France is estimated to cost around 38 months of employee compensation per person, while in Denmark or Switzerland it costs around three months. France has only two core industrial cleantech players out of approximately 60 French unicorns. China's manufacturing costs are reported to be 30 to 60 percent lower across many key energy-transition technologies. China accounts for more than 80 percent of global photovoltaic manufacturing capacity across key stages. China leads the refining of 19 out of 20 strategic minerals. Private artificial intelligence investment in the United States reached $285.9 billion in the year 2025. Private artificial intelligence investment in Europe reached $20.9 billion in the year 2025.

stories.headline: FPIs return to India stock markets with ₹53.7k cr inflows in Nov so far - Attraction point for investors? What's next?
stories.text: Foreign portfolio investors pumped ₹53,739 crore into Indian equity markets in November according to NSDL data. The recent FPI buying reduced cumulative net outflows from Indian equities to ₹2.41 lakh crore in 2026. Dr V K Vijayakumar from Geojit Investments Limited stated that aggressive foreign portfolio investor buying caused a short squeeze that pushed the Nifty up 7.58% in a week. Dr V K Vijayakumar attributed the shift in sentiment partly to a sell-off in artificial intelligence stocks in the US, South Korea, Taiwan, and Japan. Foreign investors focused their purchases on index heavyweights within the financial services, IT, automobile, and telecom sectors. Manoj Purohit from BDO India stated that expectations of favourable changes to India's capital market taxation framework encouraged foreign investors. Industry bodies have suggested the possible removal of the existing 12.5% long-term capital gains tax on foreign investors' equity investments.

stories.headline: AI slump sends investors scouring emerging markets for bargains
stories.text: Chip giants SK Hynix Inc., Samsung Electronics Co., and Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. account for almost 30% of the MSCI developing-country index. Sat Duhra of Janus Henderson Investors stated on Friday that he is adding higher-yielding stocks in China and Hong Kong. The Nasdaq 100 Index tumbled 6.4% on Thursday due to fears surrounding artificial intelligence data center builds. The MSCI developing-nations benchmark trades at approximately 8 times forecast earnings over the next 12 months. India’s NSE Nifty 50 Index jumped 2% on Friday to cap its best week since 2021. Bing Yuan at Edmond de Rothschild noted that BeOne Medicines Ltd. has advanced 37% in 2026. Wuxi Biologics Cayman Inc. has rallied 58% according to Bing Yuan.

stories.headline: Young people in UK hit by ‘low-gear economy’, warns Bank of England deputy
stories.text: Clare Lombardelli stated that the war involving Iran has caused higher energy prices and increased youth unemployment in Britain. Clare Lombardelli described the British labor market as a low-gear economy where employers freeze new recruitment instead of making redundancies. UK unemployment increased this year to 4.7%, with youth unemployment rising at a sharper rate to reach levels not seen since 2015 outside the Covid pandemic. The number of young people in the UK who are not in education, employment or training has increased to almost a million. Clare Lombardelli joined the majority of the Bank of England monetary policy committee in voting to lift the base rate from 3.75% to 4%. Clare Lombardelli stated that a further quarter-point interest rate rise could be warranted as early as the next policy meeting in December. Oil prices fell sharply to below $100 a barrel following Democratic victories in the US Congress.

stories.headline: Qantas Airways to outsource 850 head-office jobs to Accenture, services to be largely delivered from India
stories.text: Australian airline Qantas will outsource about 850 head-office jobs to technology company Accenture under a multi-year agreement. Most of the outsourced services will be delivered by Accenture teams in India, with some handled in Australia. The first implementation phase is expected by mid-2027 and will cover finance, procurement, people and marketing functions. Qantas Chief Executive Officer Vanessa Hudson stated that the changes aim to simplify operations, improve efficiency, and prepare for artificial intelligence. The Australian Services Union criticized the outsourcing plan, raising concerns over the movement of jobs and skills overseas. ASU NSW Secretary Angus McFarland stated that the union believes most affected jobs are located at Qantas headquarters in Mascot, Sydney. ASU Assistant National Secretary Scott Cowen stated that workers were told in August that there was no plan to move Australian jobs overseas.

stories.headline: India may not see US-like rise in natural interest rates despite global yield pressures: Report
stories.text: India's natural interest rate is expected to stay stable despite rising rates in developed economies, according to a study by SBI Capital Markets. The narrowing gap between Indian and US bond yields could hinder India's reliance on foreign investments to fund its current account deficit. In the United States, the natural rate of interest is projected to increase due to rising government debt, higher borrowing costs, and shifts in global investment flows. India's natural rate is supported by a stable growth outlook, anchored inflation expectations, gradual fiscal consolidation, an improving credit profile, and recovering household savings. Inflation-driven interest rate increases accounted for about 75-85 per cent of the rise in US Treasury yields since mid-2020. The gap between inflation in India and the US has narrowed over the past decade, shrinking the difference in policy rates and government bond yields. To manage the balance of payments, the SBI Capital Markets report suggested strengthening export-led growth, encouraging foreign equity investments, and maintaining adequate foreign exchange reserves.

stories.headline: Brait’s Virgin Active to acquire Holmes Place Germany for R2.84 billion
stories.text: The cash consideration for the acquisition of Holmes Place Germany is €135 million. Holmes Place Germany has 13 large-format clubs across six cities and 84 100 members. Holmes Place Germany is forecast to generate revenue of €70.2 million for the year ending in December. Holmes Place Germany is expected to have year-on-year EBITDA growth of 27%. Following the transaction, Holmes Place Germany will contribute 14% of Virgin Active's total EBITDA. Non-South African operations will account for 56% of Virgin Active group EBITDA after the deal. Virgin Active currently operates 224 clubs across 10 countries serving more than 1 million members.

stories.headline: BNPL makes a comeback as payment apps try to fix its broken economics
stories.text: Payment apps backed by Flipkart and Razorpay, named SuperMoney and POP respectively, are reintroducing buy now, pay later services in India for young borrowers. SuperMoney launched splitStore in August, requiring an upfront payment and two remaining instalments over two months. POP receives a 20-25% commission from brands on each sale, according to founder and CEO Bhargav Errangi. SuperMoney reported that its daily purchase-value run rate surged about sixfold during festive sales compared to pre-festive levels. SuperMoney's median order value rose to ₹2,000 from ₹890 two months prior, with about 65% of shoppers younger than 25. ZestMoney shut down in December 2023 before being acquired by DMI Group, and the Reserve Bank of India ordered Simpl to halt payment operations in September 2025. Consumer durable loans at non-banking financial companies rose 56.4% year-on-year to ₹77,784 crore in August according to Reserve Bank of India data.

stories.headline: 'They will kill you too': Sonia Gandhi's turbulent journey in Indian politics
stories.text: Sonia Gandhi's mother-in-law Indira Gandhi was assassinated on 31 October 1984 by two of her Sikh bodyguards at the prime minister's residence in Delhi. Following the assassination, Rajiv Gandhi was sworn in as prime minister after party leaders asked him to take the role. Sonia Gandhi writes in her memoir Belonging: A Journey of Love that her husband Rajiv Gandhi was assassinated in 1991. Sonia Gandhi arranged private lessons with a Sanskrit scholar in January 1997 to read the Bhagavad Gita, which helped resolve her inner conflict about entering politics. After leading Congress to victory in the 2004 general election, Sonia Gandhi chose Manmohan Singh to become prime minister instead of taking the role herself. Sonia Gandhi is 79 years old and currently serves as a member of the Rajya Sabha, while Rahul Gandhi is 55 and Priyanka is 53.

stories.headline: Nvidia-backed Nscale considers delaying $35 billion IPO: Report
stories.text: British cloud provider Nscale is considering delaying its stock market listing, according to a Telegraph report on Tuesday. Executives at Nscale are evaluating whether to postpone their initial public offering efforts until next year. Microsoft recently declined an option to extend its existing agreement to rent additional computing power from Nscale at a Texas data center. London-based Nscale filed for an initial public offering in September with a goal of raising approximately $3.5 billion in funding. Nscale intends to trade on the New York Stock Exchange utilizing the ticker symbol NSCL. AI company Anthropic submitted an updated prospectus on Tuesday for its initial public offering, targeting a valuation reaching up to $1.4 trillion.

stories.headline: Zelenskyy tells Europe to hurry up and pick a rep for peace talks with Russia
stories.text: Ukraine President Volodymyr Zelenskyy stated that European countries backing Ukraine need to quickly choose a single representative for peace negotiations. Volodymyr Zelenskyy proposed that one person should hold a mandate from both European Union and non-European Union supporters such as Norway and the United Kingdom. Volodymyr Zelenskyy indicated that Europe needs to accept its negotiating representative by November at the latest. Volodymyr Zelenskyy expressed hope during a trip to Denmark on Tuesday that the representative issue would be fixed by November 19th in Germany. Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni criticized the European Union's engagement with peace talks last week as being all over the place. American officials stated during talks in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday that they want Europe fully at the table during the next negotiations.

stories.headline: Oura is acquiring medical AI chatbot startup Counsel Health
stories.text: Oura agreed to acquire Counsel Health for $625 million, as announced during its quarterly earnings. Oura expects the acquisition of Counsel Health to close before the end of the year. Counsel Health is an AI-native primary care company that delivers AI-generated responses and insights using wearable health data. Oura CEO Tom Hale stated the acquisition aims to connect wearables, clinical AI, and doctor access based on biometric data. Seventy employees from Counsel Health will join Oura, and Counsel Health CEO Muthu Alagappan will become Oura's chief clinical AI officer. Counsel Health plans to expand its network of on-demand physicians, which currently consists of about 50 people.

stories.headline: US soldier arrested in UK on suspicion of spying for Russia
stories.text: British authorities arrested an unidentified US military member in the UK on suspicion of espionage for Russia. London's Metropolitan Police stated the 41-year-old was arrested on Tuesday near Gloucester in southwest England. The suspect was arrested for allegedly violating two sections of the National Security Act 2023. UK counterterror forces collaborated with the FBI and US military on the arrest, according to the police. FBI Director Kash Patel described the espionage allegations as an important arrest of utmost concern. Officers are conducting searches at two locations in Gloucestershire while the man is in custody at a London police station.

stories.headline: US says no need for new attacks but calls Iran's peace terms 'absurd'
stories.text: US President Donald Trump stated on Monday that the war with Iran was effectively over following a White House meeting with Qatar's prime minister. Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, stated in a television interview that Iran is not currently conducting any negotiations with the United States. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio described Iran's political settlement terms as absurd and not serious during a meeting of G7 foreign ministers in Paris on Tuesday. The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps reported on Tuesday that three oil tankers caught fire after hitting mines in the Strait of Hormuz. Brent crude oil prices were down nearly 15 percent over the past week and traded at $91.37 per barrel on Tuesday. US gas prices declined by four percent over the last week.

stories.headline: Poland says Pentagon backs permanent US base, with Trump decision due in December
stories.text: Poland's defense minister stated on Tuesday that the Pentagon approved plans for a permanent United States military base in the country. President Donald Trump is anticipated to make a final decision regarding the base in early December. Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz spoke after holding discussions with United States Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth in Washington. The Pentagon's official statement did not endorse the base or confirm the December timetable while acknowledging ongoing discussions. Pete Hegseth commended the military buildup of Poland and described its army as one of the most formidable in Europe. Prime Minister Donald Tusk and President Karol Nawrocki agreed last week to cooperate in securing the proposed military base.

stories.headline: The Daily View: Does China’s shipbuilding boom contain the seeds of shipping’s next problem?
stories.text: China Merchants plans to resurrect Quanzhou Shipyard amid a global capacity shortage in the shipbuilding industry. The global shipbuilding orderbook stands at a record 226m cgt, which is valued at around $700bn. Danish Ship Finance calculates that demonstrated annual shipbuilding capacity is just 56.4m cgt. More than three-quarters of roughly 225 yard expansion projects tracked by Clarksons are located in China. Active Chinese shipyards have more than doubled since 2020, with measured capacity reaching 32m cgt or 57% of the global total. Global shipbuilding output could reach 72m cgt in the year 2028, representing double its 2020 low.

stories.headline: Explainer: What is Mawan Terminal? How China’s high-tech ports could change how 80% of global trade moves
stories.text: Western experts fear that China's expanding shipping technology could give Beijing monopolistic positions in new technologies, allowing it to coerce economies, spy on rivals, or cripple trade routes. LOGINK, a shipping data platform backed by Beijing, has collapsed according to a Reuters report. China stated in a May editorial published on its transport ministry website that whoever completes digital transformation first will gain the upper hand in global port and shipping competition. Each crane at the New Qianwan Container Terminal can handle 61 containers in an hour, which is more than double the rate achieved with traditional methods. The United States has lagged behind China in automating ports at a rapid pace due to union opposition driven by worries over job losses. Chinese companies like Westwell and Huawei are packaging smart-port technology to sell in overseas markets.

stories.headline: US officials seek ‘final end’ to Russia-Ukraine war, as Abu Dhabi talks set to continue
stories.text: United States officials stated they are seeking a final end to the Russia-Ukraine war as trilateral peace talks began in Abu Dhabi. The Ukrainian president, Volodymyr Zelenskyy, described the first day of discussions as constructive and fairly substantive regarding security guarantees. Part of the Donald Trump administration proposal involves creating a new long-term security architecture between Russia and Europe. European officials held separate discussions on Tuesday with representatives from Ukraine and the United States concerning future arrangements and sovereignty. The US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, stated it is a goal to eventually expand the Russia-US-Ukraine talks to include other European voices. A United States administration official mentioned that negotiators could potentially lift sanctions against Russia to reach a deal.

stories.headline: Bharat Mobility 3.0 to see 50 countries, 1,750+ exhibitors on February 4-9, 2027
stories.text: The third Bharat Mobility Global Expo is scheduled to take place from February 4 to 9, 2027, featuring participation from more than 50 countries. Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal stated that over 25,000 foreign visitors and more than 10-lakh total visitors are expected to attend the event. The upcoming expo will host over 1,750 exhibitors and feature more than 239 product launches. Countries participating in the mega show include the US, China, Japan, Mexico, Sri Lanka, Germany, Italy, Spain, and Taiwan. The 2027 expo will be held across two venues, namely Bharat Mandapam from February 4-9 and Yashobhoomi from February 4-7. The Bharat Mobility Global Expo 2027 will comprise 11 concurrent shows, newly incorporating Agri-Mobility Solutions, and Metro and Urban Mass Transit.

stories.headline: ‘Flying cars’ could launch in China next summer, maker of two-seat model says
stories.text: XPeng chief executive Deli Zhao stated that flying cars could launch in China by the second half of 2027. The two-seater XPeng low-altitude vehicle is priced at $300,000. The flying vehicle has been approved by civil aviation authorities in China for limited use. The XPeng vehicle features six drone-like battery-powered propellers and a joystick for steering. The purchase price of the XPeng vehicle includes a six-wheel van comparable in size to a Ford Transit. The XPeng flying vehicle has a flight range of 30km, which equates to 18.6 miles.

stories.headline: India’s rice procurement down by 19 lakh tonne in October due to poor arrivals
stories.text: Rice procurement for the 2026-27 season dropped to about 104 lakh tonnes in October from over 123 lakh tonnes a year earlier. Punjab purchased 73.52 lakh tonnes of rice until October 31, compared to 72.98 lakh tonnes in the previous year. Haryana procured 26.25 lakh tonnes of rice, registering a drop from 38.79 lakh tonnes in the previous year. The government has set a target to buy 715.22 lakh tonnes of paddy from the kharif-grown crop in the 2026-27 marketing season. Farmers attributed the lower paddy arrivals in these states to lower crops and reduced yields. Paddy acreage in the kharif season ended lower at 433.62 lakh hectares as of October 2 against 449.18 lakh hectares a year ago.

stories.headline: IAEA Condemns Deadly Drone Attack Near Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia Nuclear Power Plant
stories.text: A drone attack near Ukraine's Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant resulted in the deaths of two employees, including one from the nuclear facility and one from a neighbouring thermal power plant. Rafael Grossi, Director General of the International Atomic Energy Agency, described the attacks as unacceptable in a message posted on X. Rafael Grossi stated that the attacks violate the indispensable pillars of nuclear safety and must cease immediately. Ukraine and Russia regularly accuse each other of targeting the Zaporizhzhia nuclear power plant site, which is close to the front line. The Zaporizhzhia nuclear facility has been occupied by Russia since March 2022 and is the largest nuclear facility in Europe. All six reactors at the Zaporizhzhia nuclear facility have been shut down since 2022, and International Atomic Energy Agency teams have been present on site since September 2022.

stories.headline: Matrimony.com to acquire 50% stake in astrology tech firm Astro-Vision, reports Q2 PAT up nearly 3X
stories.text: The board of Matrimony.com approved acquiring an additional 50 percent stake in Astro-Vision Futuretech Private Ltd for approximately ₹8 crore. Matrimony.com already holds a 26.09 percent stake in Astro-Vision, bringing its total stake to 76.09 percent after the acquisition. Astro-Vision recorded a revenue of ₹20.57 crore in FY26. Matrimony.com reported a profit after tax of ₹21 crore for the quarter ended September 2026, compared to ₹7.8 crore in the same period last year. Matrimony.com reported a revenue from operations increase of 18.4 percent to ₹135 crore. Matrimony.com reported billings increased 10.7 percent year-on-year to ₹131 crore.

stories.headline: Orkla India posts 19 per cent rise in Q2 profit to Rs 91 crore
stories.text: Orkla India reported a consolidated revenue of Rs 776.16 crore for Q2 FY27, which is up 19.4 per cent year-on-year. Orkla India registered a consolidated profit after tax of Rs 91.42 crore for the quarter ended September 2026. Orkla India posted consolidated earnings per share of Rs 6.70 for Q2 FY27, compared with Rs 5.60 in Q2 FY26. Orkla India achieved a positive consolidated cash flow from operating activities of Rs 108.19 crore for the first half of FY27. Orkla India included an exceptional item of Rs 1.5 crore in the six-month period due to the impact of India’s new Labour Codes. Orkla India board approved the unaudited results on 4 November 2026, which were signed by managing director and chief executive officer Sanjay Sharma.

stories.headline: Qantas to bring 850 jobs to India via outsourcing deal with Accenture; Aussie unions raise concerns: Report
stories.text: Qantas plans to outsource 850 head office jobs to Accenture under a multi-year agreement, with most assigned to India. Qantas CEO Vanessa Hudson announced the outsourcing plan in an internal staff email. Qantas stated the outsourcing aims to modernise technology and prepare the business for artificial intelligence. The changes will begin by the middle of next year, initially covering finance, procurement, people and marketing functions. Qantas intends to redeploy some employees by reskilling and retraining them for other internal roles. ASU NSW Secretary Angus McFarland criticized the move as offshoring Australian jobs and skills.

stories.headline: Electric Car Sales In India Increase By 76% In October
stories.text: India’s electric passenger vehicle retail sales increased 76.47% year-on-year to 37,049 units in October 2026, according to the Federation of Automobile Dealers Associations. Electric passenger vehicles accounted for 7.3% of total passenger vehicle retail sales in October 2026, up from 3.5% in October 2025. Tata Motors led India’s electric passenger vehicle market with 14,669 retail sales in October 2026, marking a 77.61% increase year-on-year. Mahindra secured the second position in India's electric car sales with 8,538 units, achieving 85.65% year-on-year growth in October 2026. MG ranked third in electric car sales with 5,939 units, registering 10.8% annual growth in October 2026. VinFast took the fourth position with 2,571 units in October 2026, growing more than 1,700% year-on-year from 142 units in October 2025.

stories.headline: Faisal Islam: What the boss of US tech giant Nvidia told me about China and national security
stories.text: Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang is currently being investigated regarding an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. Nvidia is led by Jensen Huang, and its technology is rooted in repurposed games graphics and Taiwan's manufacturing prowess. Jensen Huang attempted to get US President Donald Trump to lift export bans to China on some of the highest performing AI chips, specifically the H200. Nvidia has actual hard revenues of about $400bn this year. Nvidia experienced a Monday drop of about 4% of its value reflecting new and extraordinary risks at this junction of tech and global politics. The chipmaker Nvidia is still worth more than $4 trillion.

stories.headline: Apple introduces $50 AI usage packs for Creator Studio apps: What users get and how they work
stories.text: Apple introduced a paid option named Intelligence Usage Pack for Creator Studio applications at a cost of $49.99 as a one-time purchase. The paid pack allows users to continue accessing supported artificial intelligence tools after exhausting their free monthly allowance. The feature was initially launched with the recent Logic Pro update and will expand to Final Cut Pro, Pixelmator Pro, and the iWork suite in November 2026. According to Apple's technical support page, the pack is a single purchase that carries over from month to month and expires 12 months after purchase. The additional usage packs are associated with the Apple Account used to make the purchase and are not available for Family Sharing. Apple has included India alongside eight other countries including the US, the UK, Canada, Brazil, France, Germany, and Mexico for purchasing the extra pack.

stories.headline: Sensex, Nifty 50 rise over 6% in past 5 sessions: More rally from tomorrow or profit booking will dent returns hopes?
stories.text: The Sensex and the Nifty 50 surged over 6% in the past five trading sessions leading up to Wednesday's trading session. On Monday, November 9, the Sensex advanced 107.25 points to close at 81,106.65, and the Nifty 50 gained 58.25 points to settle at 25,044.65. Brent crude prices fell nearly 14% last week to around $99 per barrel. Foreign investors purchased Indian shares worth more than $4.1 billion in November. Citi raised its end-2027 Nifty target to 28,000, which implies about 12% upside from the November 9 closing level. HSBC upgraded its rating on Indian equities to 'overweight' from 'neutral'.

stories.headline: India launches probe into dumping of aluminium products from China, Malaysia, Vietnam
stories.text: India's Directorate General of Trade Remedies has launched suo-motu anti-dumping probes into aluminium products from China, Malaysia, Vietnam, and Thailand. The Directorate General of Trade Remedies initiated the investigation to guard MSME units against cheap imports from these countries. The Aluminium Extrusion Manufacturers Association of India, representing 228 manufacturers, submitted representations to the Directorate General of Trade Remedies. The Directorate General of Trade Remedies issued the notification to initiate the anti-dumping investigation on November 9. The Directorate General of Trade Remedies will determine the existence and effect of dumping and recommend the appropriate anti-dumping duty amount. The Indian finance ministry holds the authority to make the final decision regarding the imposition of duties.

stories.headline: EU manufacturers could give up on competing with China by 2030, warns commerce chief
stories.text: European Union Chamber of Commerce in China head Jens Eskelund warned that European manufacturers could stop trying to compete with Chinese counterparts by the end of the decade. Jens Eskelund stated that the European Union is facing a record trade deficit running at £1bn (€1.18bn) a day with China. Goldman Sachs forecasted that Chinese exports would reduce the European Union gross domestic product by 0.5% and Germany's by up to 0.9% by the end of the decade. BMW reported a 22% drop in China sales during the first nine months of the year and issued its second profit warning of the year. Jens Eskelund noted that the trade imbalance cannot be resolved by increasing exports, with China's surplus against the rest of the world expected to exceed $1.2tn (£900bn). Jens Eskelund pointed out that European companies struggle to compete against Chinese supply chains partly due to a currency undervalued by about 30%.

stories.headline: Asian Stocks Rise on CoreWeave Results, Bonds Drop: Markets Wrap
stories.text: Asian stocks increased during early trading sessions following positive financial results reported by CoreWeave Inc. CoreWeave Inc. reported better-than-expected earnings that alleviated worries regarding the future trajectory of the artificial intelligence trade. The positive movement in Asian stocks helped offset a previous selloff on Wall Street. The Wall Street selloff was driven by inflation in the United States coming in higher than anticipated.

stories.headline: BoE's Lombardelli Sees Case for Another Rate Hike as Persistent Inflation Conditions Take Shape - News and Statistics
stories.text: Bank of England Deputy Governor Clare Lombardelli stated that conditions for persistent inflation in Britain are taking shape. Clare Lombardelli stated she would not rule December or February in or out for upcoming Monetary Policy Committee meetings. Clare Lombardelli described Britain's labour market as being in low gear with reduced rates of hiring and job turnover. Clare Lombardelli highlighted that the unemployment rate had risen more for younger workers aged 18 to 24 compared with other workers.

stories.headline: Gold Holds Loss Near $4,000 on Hot US Inflation, Fed Remarks
stories.text: Gold retained its price decreases following a high United States inflation report and hawkish comments from Federal Reserve officials. The economic data and Federal Reserve comments strengthened expectations for an interest rate hike in December.

stories.headline: Barrick Mining Files for IPO of North American Gold Assets
stories.text: Barrick Mining Corp. is planning an initial public offering for its North American gold business in the United States. John Thornton is serving as the long-time Chairman of Barrick Mining Corp.

stories.headline: Gold Fields Ltd Stock (GFI) Moved Down by 7.54% on Nov 10: A Full Analysis
stories.text: Top sector stocks Newmont Corporation, Freeport-McMoRan Inc, and James Hardie Industries PLC fell by 4.39%, 3.74%, and 3.69% respectively. Multiple analysts rated Gold Fields Ltd as Buy over the past month with an average price target of $47.36.

stories.headline: We Think You Should Be Aware Of Some Concerning Factors In Vigor Plast India's (NSE:VIGOR) Earnings
stories.text: Vigor Plast India recorded an accrual ratio of 0.42 for the year leading up to September 2026. Vigor Plast India failed to produce any free cash flow during the period. Vigor Plast India posted negative free cash flow of ₹84m over the last year. Vigor Plast India reported a statutory profit of ₹96.1m over the last year. Vigor Plast India also had negative free cash flow during the previous year.

stories.headline: Linde India's (NSE:LINDEINDIA) Shareholders Have More To Worry About Than Only Soft Earnings
stories.text: Linde India Limited's market responded positively to the recent earnings report despite lackluster headline numbers. For the year to September 2026, Linde India Limited recorded an accrual ratio of 0.26. Linde India Limited reported a statutory profit of ₹4.94b in the last twelve months. Linde India Limited experienced a cash burn and negative free cash flow with an outflow of ₹6.8b in the last twelve months. Linde India Limited achieved an 18% per annum growth in EPS for the last three years.

stories.headline: Ericsson, HBL Validate 5G SA for India’s Kavach 4.0 Railway Safety System
stories.text: Ericsson and HBL successfully integrated Kavach 4.0, India's SIL-4 certified automatic train protection system, with a 5G network environment at HBL's R&D laboratory in Hyderabad. The collaboration evaluates the role of 5G Standalone in next-generation railway communications and supports higher speeds on mainline railways. Kavach 4.0 provides capabilities that improve safety and security while enabling higher train speeds as traffic density increases. The collaboration enables Ericsson and HBL to validate their integration and interoperability in a laboratory environment. Mayank Bhargava is the Director of Emerging Business and Public Sector at Ericsson India.

stories.headline: US House Republicans block Pete Hegseth impeachment effort
stories.text: United States House of Representatives Republicans blocked an effort to advance the impeachment of Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth on Tuesday. The lower house of the United States Congress voted in favour of a motion to refer impeachment charges to the House Judiciary Committee. The procedural vote on Tuesday resulted in 211 in favour and 204 against the motion. Representative Thomas Massie was the sole Republican who voted against the procedural motion. Thomas Massie introduced eight separate articles of impeachment accusing Pete Hegseth of launching an illegal war against Iran without congressional approval.

stories.headline: Sony cancels live-service shooter Fairgames
stories.text: Sony canceled the heist game Fairgames, which was originally announced in 2023. The cancellation of Fairgames will not lead to any job cuts. Developer Haven Studios will transition to supporting other PlayStation studios following the cancellation. Fairgames was canceled after player feedback and retention results from a recent test missed established goals. Sony acquired Haven Studios in the year 2022.

stories.headline: Japan's Cosmo Energy eyes steady Middle East oil imports for 2027 despite disruptions
stories.text: Japan's third-biggest oil refiner Cosmo Energy Holdings is negotiating 2027 crude term contracts with Middle Eastern oil producers to maintain this year's volumes, as stated by Senior Executive Officer Tomoki Iwai on Tuesday. Tomoki Iwai stated that Cosmo Energy Holdings has sourced roughly equal volumes of crude from the Middle East and regions like the US and Mexico since the April-June first quarter of fiscal 2026. Tomoki Iwai reported that Cosmo Energy Holdings has secured crude supplies through January and relies mainly on ship-to-ship transfers at sea because chartered tankers cannot transit the Strait of Hormuz or Bab el-Mandeb. Cosmo Energy Holdings plans to source crude mainly from the Middle East and likely shift back to regional supplies once the straits reopen, Tomoki Iwai said. Cosmo Energy Holdings reported that its net profit for the April-September period rose more than sixfold to JPY147 billion, or $931 million, driven by higher inventory appraisal gains and stronger refining margins, while the refinery utilisation rate was 92.8 per cent.

stories.headline: Russian naval aggression prompts new defensive initiative with ‘beer-drinking nations’
stories.text: British naval activity surrounding the UK involving Russian vessels has risen by 41% during the initial nine months of the year according to British defence readiness minister Luke Pollard. A maritime defensive initiative known as the Northern Navies Initiative brings together the UK, the Netherlands, and Baltic and Nordic countries to integrate sea drones with warships. Chancellor John Healey allocated an extra £10bn a year to defence in 2030 during October's budget. A £1.5bn investment in sea drones spanning four years was included in the defence investment plan funded in the October budget. An additional amount of £90m is designated for underwater drones and sensors monitoring the Greenland-Iceland-UK gap.

stories.headline: China blocks SoftBank’s $5.4 billion takeover of ABB Robotics
stories.text: China has blocked SoftBank Group's proposed $5.4 billion acquisition of ABB's robotics business following a government review on national security grounds. ABB confirmed the decision on November 5 after being informed that China's Office of the Working Mechanism for Foreign Investment Security Review prohibited the transaction in China. SoftBank Group stated on November 6 that it received notification of the prohibition on November 4 and is continuing discussions with ABB. China is ABB Robotics' largest market, with more than 90 percent of the robots supplied to Chinese customers manufactured locally. ABB opened a $150 million robotics manufacturing facility in Shanghai in 2022 and has operated in China for decades.

stories.headline: Merz accused of ‘blackmail’ by Slovak PM after demand for Ukraine aid in EU budget
stories.text: German chancellor Friedrich Merz stated he will block the European Union's seven-year budget unless an agreement on financial aid for Ukraine is reached. Slovakia prime minister Robert Fico accused Friedrich Merz of blackmail in response to the budget block threat. The European Union agreed last year to lend Ukraine €90bn to cover two-thirds of military and civilian costs for 2026 and 2027. Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelenskyy requested €70bn to address a budget shortfall caused by ongoing bombardment. Friedrich Merz previously attempted to utilize €210bn of Russian sovereign wealth frozen in the European Union, but opposition led by Belgium halted the plan.

stories.headline: US team visits Delhi to advance technical aspects of India-US trade pact
stories.text: A two-member US team on customs and trade facilitation visited New Delhi to advance technical aspects of the India-US bilateral trade agreement. The US team was in New Delhi on November 2-3 to progress the technical part of the negotiations. The visit of the US team occurred during the US midterm elections where Democrats secured control of both the Senate and the House of Representatives. Technical discussions on the proposed pact were anticipated to persist despite the Republican loss, though clarity on the future course of the trade deal remained absent. India and the US are negotiating the bilateral trade agreement while differences over tariff levels and access to Indian agricultural and dairy markets stall an interim agreement.

stories.headline: India demands unimpeded Hormuz shipping, pledges full support for detained Captain Ajay Pant
stories.text: India called for safe and unimpeded navigation through the Strait of Hormuz during a media briefing on November 10. Indian Merchant Navy Captain Ajay Pant is currently held in judicial custody in the United Kingdom. British forces intercepted the oil tanker MV Smyrtos on June 14 over alleged breaches of Russian oil sanctions. Captain Ajay Pant received a visit from his wife on November 9 as part of ongoing consular assistance. Approximately 20% of global petroleum passes through the Strait of Hormuz according to details on the energy chokepoint.

stories.headline: Ferrexpo pauses iron ore output as Ukraine power crisis deepens
stories.text: Ferrexpo has temporarily suspended iron ore production at its Ukrainian operations because of power supply disruptions caused by attacks on electricity infrastructure. Ferrexpo confirmed that its own assets did not suffer any physical damage from the attacks. Ferrexpo management has not provided a timetable for the resumption of production. Ferrexpo is able to fulfil orders from European customers using its existing inventories. Broker Peel Hunt placed its investment recommendation and share price target for Ferrexpo under review.

stories.headline: Army turns to MSMEs and start-ups for critical combat spares as defence PSUs fall short
stories.text: The Indian Army is approaching private MSMEs and start-ups to manufacture combat critical spares and sub-assemblies for tanks like the T-72 and T-90s. The Master General Sustenance branch plans to share a compendium of 300 different types of critical spares with the domestic industry. The Indian Army previously shared a compendium of 200 spares and components with the Society of Indian Defence Manufacturers on August 18. The Army's Indigenisation Directorate opened up a list of 375 specific parts in 2025 for defence companies to innovate and produce. Out of roughly 450,000 total spares identified, the Indian Army is actively working to indigenise some 50,000 critical items.

stories.headline: ‘Flying blind’: Why experts fear Treasury’s China biotech investment crackdown will backfire
stories.text: The U.S. Department of the Treasury proposed rules to implement the Comprehensive Outbound Investment National Security Act, aiming to add pharmaceutical compounds to an outbound investment blacklist targeting China. Peter Kolchinsky, managing partner at RA Capital, stated that the proposed restrictions would cripple American innovation, hand dominance to Europe and China, and leave investors flying blind. RA Capital and a coalition of industry leaders published a formal comment letter warning that the proposed rule constrains only American companies while allowing foreign competitors to scoop up Chinese clinical assets. The Treasury draft policy avoids banning straightforward, cash-based drug licensing deals but casts an ambiguous net over equity investments, co-development arrangements, and joint ventures with Chinese entities. Deborah Curtis, a partner at Arnold & Porter, explained that COINS restrictions apply to any U.S. person, making it easier for foreign firms to evade them by cutting Americans out of the loop.

stories.headline: India’s 2026-27 apple imports may increase 19% to 5.11 lakh tonne on rising demand
stories.text: The USDA Foreign Agricultural Service office in New Delhi forecasts India's apple imports to rise by 19 percent to 5.11 lakh tonnes during the 2026-27 marketing year. The USDA Foreign Agricultural Service office in New Delhi revised the apple import estimate for 2025-26 to 4.28 lakh tonnes. The USDA Foreign Agricultural Service office in New Delhi expects India's apple consumption to increase by 5 percent to 2.91 million tonnes in 2026-27. The USDA Foreign Agricultural Service office in New Delhi forecasts a 3 percent growth in apple production for 2026-27 to 2.59 million tonnes. stories.headline: Ukraine war: US energy deal with Russia undermines Western alliance
stories.text: In October, United States President Donald Trump announced a sanctions waiver for Russian oil allowing the supply of over two million barrels of diesel to global markets. Jonathan Hafetz of the IBA Human Rights Law Committee stated that the oil deal undermines United States sanctions effectiveness by increasing Russian oil export revenues. The United States government defended the decision by arguing it makes Russia more likely to come to the negotiating table to end the war in Ukraine. In March, the United States issued a 30-day general licence allowing the sale and delivery of Russian sebroane crude oil which was renewed twice and lasted until June. House and Senate Democrats sent letters to major United States banks asking them to preserve records relating to diesel imports under the waiver.

stories.headline: Surely India has a promising hand to play: Anand Mahindra on nations compelling AI opportunity
stories.text: Mahindra Group Chairman Anand Mahindra stated on Tuesday that India has a compelling artificial intelligence opportunity. Anand Mahindra highlighted India's software talent, systems integration expertise, and enormous domestic market for artificial intelligence use cases in a post on X. Anand Mahindra suggested that renewed global investor interest in Indian equities may have more staying power than previously thought. Anand Mahindra noted that Stanford University ranks India third globally in artificial intelligence vibrancy. Anand Mahindra acknowledged that India does not manufacture the most advanced chips or lead the race in foundational large language models.

stories.headline: India’s unemployment rate falls to 5.1% in July-September quarter as rural joblessness declines
stories.text: India's unemployment rate fell to 5.1 per cent in the July-September 2026 quarter from 5.4 per cent in the previous quarter, according to government data released on Tuesday. The Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation reported that rural unemployment dropped to 4.3 per cent from 4.8 per cent in the April-June 2026 period. Urban unemployment in India increased slightly to 6.8 per cent during the July-September 2026 quarter compared to 6.7 per cent in the prior quarter. The proportion of Indian women working or looking for jobs increased to 34.7 per cent in July-September 2026 from 33.2 per cent previously. The share of rural workers engaged in agriculture in India rose to 56.7 per cent in July-September 2026 from 52.9 per cent in the previous quarter.

stories.headline: Ukraine’s fiber-optic drones get squeezed by AI data center demand
stories.text: Ukraine and Russia have produced an estimated 50,000 fiber-optic drones per month in recent years. Russia imported 328,000 miles of fiber-optic cable from China in August 2025, compared to Ukraine getting just 72 miles. TrendForce projected a worldwide shortfall of 111 million miles or 180 million kilometers of fiber-optic cable in 2026 due to the global AI boom and data center buildout. Oleksiy, an R&D representative for Ukrainian drone manufacturer BlueBird Tech, stated that fiber-optic prices increased by roughly six to 10 times between 2025 and 2026. Oleksiy noted that the most difficult period regarding prices and shortages occurred around March.

stories.headline: ​U.S. B&M Defense Tests AA Lancer 7 Interceptor Drones in Ukraine (Video)
stories.text: The American defense company B&M Defense tested its AA Lancer 7 interceptor drone in Ukraine. The AA Lancer 7 drone is designed to reach a maximum speed of 400 km/h. The manufacturer states that the AA Lancer 7 has a cruising speed of 180 km/h and a maximum range of 30 kilometers. B&M Defense transferred a number of AA Lancer 7 interceptor drones to units of the Defense Forces of Ukraine for combat testing. B&M Defense stated it is developing interceptor drones to counter jet-powered aerial threats.

stories.headline: Olectra Greentech Q2 Results: Profit Jumps 104% QoQ; Company Sells 34% Stake in Evey Trans (UJJ)
stories.text: On Monday, the Nifty 50 closed at 25,044.65, up 0.23%, and the Sensex ended 0.13% higher at 81,106.65. Olectra Greentech Ltd. shares closed at Rs. 1,079.50 on the NSE, marking an increase of about 2.03 percent from the previous close of 1,058. stories.headline: From curry puffs to medicated oil: Singapore heritage brands look to China at Shanghai expo
stories.text: Heritage Tanglin Puff made its debut at the annual China International Import Expo in Shanghai, which ran from Nov 5 to 10. Heritage Tanglin Puff sold out all 4,000 puffs by Nov 9, a day before the expo closed. Heritage Tanglin Puff sold its curry puffs at 12 yuan or S$2.30 each during the Shanghai expo. See Hai Tat Medical Hall priced its roll-on aroma oil at 39 yuan each for the Chinese market. Singapore businesses have generated a cumulative trade value of $533 million through the event since the inaugural CIIE in 2018.

stories.headline: FPIs turn net buyers in November, pump ₹53,739 crore into Indian equities
stories.text: Foreign Portfolio Investors became net buyers of Indian equities in November after two consecutive months of outflows. Foreign Portfolio Investors infused Rs 53,739 crore into Indian equities during the first nine days of November. Cumulative Foreign Portfolio Investor outflows from Indian equities in 2026 reached Rs 2.41 trillion. Foreign Portfolio Investors bought heavily in index heavyweights including financial services, information technology, automobiles, and telecom sectors. Foreign investors invested Rs 7,759 crore in the debt segment through the Fully Accessible Route.

stories.headline: NMDC in talks with Russia’s Rosatom to explore lithium mining and processing opportunities
stories.text: NMDC officials visited Russia last month to attend a conference and held discussions with state nuclear firm Rosatom. A spokesperson for Rosatom stated that the Russian company was not currently engaged in talks with NMDC. India currently meets its lithium demand primarily through imports from China, Vietnam and Ecuador. Rosatom and Russian miner Nornickel are developing Russia's largest lithium deposit through their Polar Lithium joint venture. Commercial production at the Polar Lithium joint venture is expected to begin by 2030.

stories.headline: Govts investing heavily in bioeconomy; India best example of demand, supply growing together: WEF
stories.text: The World Economic Forum stated on Tuesday that global governments are investing heavily in bioeconomy development, with India serving as the clearest example of demand and supply growing together. The World Economic Forum reported that India possesses the most cross-cutting portfolio, with 48 per cent of policy instruments dedicated to enabling conditions like research and development, tax incentives, and institutional capacity. India recorded the highest combined share of policy instruments at 76 per cent, followed by the United Kingdom at 69 per cent, Brazil at 68 per cent, and the United States at 67 per cent. India achieved 20 per cent ethanol blending five years ahead of the original 2030 target by pairing the Ethanol Blended Petrol Programme with concessional finance through the Ethanol Interest Subvention Scheme. The Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas reported cumulative emissions savings of 95.2 million tonne of carbon dioxide from the ethanol initiative, though this figure lacks independent evaluation.

stories.headline: China's first nuclear power project with private investment progresses in Zhejiang
stories.text: Full-scale construction of the second phase of the Zhejiang San'ao Nuclear Power Project began on Tuesday in Zhejiang Province. Private capital investment in the second phase of the Zhejiang San'ao Nuclear Power Project increased to 10 percent. The Zhejiang San'ao Nuclear Power Project is located in Cangnan County in Wenzhou and utilizes Hualong One third-generation reactors. Nearly 300 million euros, equivalent to about 336.3 million U.S. dollars, has been allocated for the extended period of the EU mission. stories.headline: Ferrexpo Temporarily Suspends Iron Ore Production Following Attacks on Ukraine’s Electricity Infrastructure
stories.text: Ferrexpo plc temporarily suspended production at its Ukrainian operations because of attacks on the country's electricity infrastructure. Damage to electricity transmission lines and substations caused an unstable power supply insufficient for Ferrexpo plc production. Ferrexpo plc stated that its production assets did not sustain any damage from the latest attacks. Ferrexpo plc remains able to supply European customers using existing inventory stockpiles despite the production suspension. Ferrexpo plc has not provided a timetable for the resumption of operations or disclosed the potential financial impact.

stories.headline: ITC, Power Grid, ONGC, Coal India, SBI Life: Nifty stocks trade near 52-week lows; what's next?
stories.text: ITC shares fell 1.66% on Monday to trade at Rs 278.50, with a market capitalisation of Rs 3.49 lakh crore. Axis Securities reduced its target price for ITC to Rs 260 from Rs 285 due to higher cigarette taxes, rising energy costs, and supply-chain issues. Nuvama upgraded Power Grid to 'BUY' and raised its target price to Rs 300 from Rs 283. MOFSL lowered its domestic production estimates for ONGC for FY27 and FY28 to 39.2 mmt and 39.9 mmt respectively. SBI Life Insurance Company shares ended 1.41% lower at Rs 1745 on Monday, bringing its market capitalisation to Rs 1.75 lakh crore.

stories.headline: Fed’s Paulson Says Gradual Tightening Seems Appropriate for Now
stories.text: Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia President Anna Paulson stated she supports a slow pace for raising interest rates. Anna Paulson noted that wage pressures have remained restricted. Anna Paulson mentioned that inflation expectations stay aligned with the central bank goal of 2%.

stories.headline: Stifel CEO on Anthropic, Integrating AI and Fed Policy
stories.text: Stifel announced a new partnership with Anthropic during the 2026 Blueprint Conference held in Las Vegas. Stifel CEO and Chairman Ron Kruszewski stated the AI tools are designed to help advisers organize work, improve productivity, and communicate with clients. Ron Kruszewski discussed Federal Reserve monetary policy and current market conditions during an appearance on Bloomberg The Close.

stories.headline: Nasdaq Falls 0.74% as Sticky US October Inflation Stokes December Rate-Hike Bets, Nvidia Extends Drop Over 5%
stories.text: Nvidia fell 5.53% to $168.78 amid an independent investigation into Jensen Huang concerning media reports that he may have been targeted by foreign intelligence operations. stories.headline: Fed's Bowman Warns About Potential Impact of AI Bets Not Panning Out
stories.text: Federal Reserve Governor Michelle Bowman stated that financial markets face risks to economic activity, which includes a potential sharp downturn in stock prices. Michelle Bowman warned that stock prices could drop sharply if returns on investments in artificial intelligence fail to meet expectations. Michelle Bowman made her comments during an appearance at an event hosted by the Council on Foreign Relations.

stories.headline: Daily summary: CPI reading hits markets, hawkish Fed and Wall Street selloff
stories.text: Wall Street faced strong selling pressure following the release of consumer price index inflation data. The Federal Reserve issued hawkish signals following the inflation data release. The US dollar posted its strongest appreciation session since September.

stories.headline: Brazil Central Bank Signals Caution on Price Rise, Slowdown
stories.text: Brazil's central bank stated it will maintain a cautious approach as inflationary pressures continue to grow in the economy. Brazil's central bank reported that high interest rates are placing an increasing burden on economic activity. Brazil's central bank noted that supply shocks are contributing to higher prices.

stories.headline: Rate-Hike Debate Ignited by Fed Officials as CPI Comes in Hot
stories.text: Federal Reserve officials have opened the possibility of more aggressive interest-rate increases in the coming months. The potential for rate hikes follows faster-than-expected inflation recorded in October. The higher October inflation injected new urgency into the central bank's efforts to tame prices.

stories.headline: Petrobras Earnings Disappoint Despite Oil, Refining Tailwinds
stories.text: Brazil state-controlled oil producer Petrobras missed third-quarter earnings estimates despite record oil and gas production.

stories.text: Newmont generates revenue from major gold assets including Peñasquito, Boddington, and NGM.

stories.headline: Pixel phones getting new icon styles, Create My Widget, and more in November Pixel Drop
stories.text: Google is rolling out a new quarterly Pixel Drop update for Pixel phones. Google is expanding Gemini artificial intelligence features from the Pixel 11 to the Pixel 10 lineup, excluding the budget-oriented Pixel 10a. The Pixel 10 series is receiving improved personalized suggestions previously known as Magic Cue, Rambler AI-assisted voice input, and Gemini app automation. Google has moved AI-powered icon theming to a Nano Banana model to unlock 10 new icon styles. Google is introducing Create My Widget to Pixel phones, allowing Android to build home screen widgets based on user descriptions. Google Messages on Pixel 11 phones is receiving HiLight support to illuminate messages from important contacts. Google Pixel Watch 3 and newer models will display step-by-step guidance for workouts and log reps and weights.

stories.headline: Nvidia (NVDA) Reports Next Week: Wall Street Expects Earnings Growth
stories.text: Nvidia is expected to report its results for the quarter ended October 2026 on November 17. Nvidia is expected to post quarterly earnings of $2.49 per share, representing a year-over-year change of +91.5%. Revenues for Nvidia are expected to reach $108.99 billion, marking a 91.2% increase from the year-ago quarter. Nvidia holds an Earnings ESP of -0.55% because the Most Accurate Estimate is lower than the Zacks Consensus Estimate. Nvidia currently carries a Zacks Rank of #2. For the last reported quarter, Nvidia was expected to post earnings of $2.09 per share but actually produced earnings of $2.22. Nvidia has beaten consensus EPS estimates in each of the trailing four quarters.

stories.headline: 6 Members of Congress Set for 'Broadband and AI' as Reps. Pramila Jayapal and Jennifer McClellan Join Keynote Lineup
stories.text: Representatives Pramila Jayapal and Jennifer McClellan will deliver keynotes at the Broadband and AI in the Next Congress conference. stories.headline: Nvidia hires Wachtell Lipton for Jensen Huang investigation
stories.text: Nvidia hired the law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to lead an investigation concerning CEO and co-founder Jensen Huang. Law firm partner Joon H. Kim will lead the probe into Jensen Huang. The Nvidia board of directors launched the independent investigation on Sunday. Jensen Huang was targeted over reports of a romantic relationship with Alice Huang, a former Megaspeed executive alleged to be a Chinese spy. Alice Huang was alleged in an October New York Times report to have ties to Chinese intelligence and helped funnel advanced Nvidia chips to China. Jensen Huang admitted to an affair in a message to the company on Sunday and pledged to cooperate with the investigation.

stories.headline: Short seller flagged Jensen Huang’s 'uncomfortably close' ties to alleged Chinese spy months ago
stories.text: Culper Research published a report titled Nvidia The China Problem in May 2026 highlighting ties between Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang and Alice Huang. Culper Research alleged that Megaspeed, a Singapore-based chip buyer where Alice Huang worked, was financed by Alibaba through shell companies. Culper Research stated it held a short position in Nvidia because of geopolitical tensions and export controls imposed by the United States. Culper Research claimed that Chinese firms continue accessing advanced Nvidia chips through diversion from buyers located in Southeast Asia. Nvidia Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang stated over the weekend that he was unfaithful to his wife and deeply sorry. Nvidia established an independent investigation led by a committee of independent directors and outside counsel to examine the matter.

stories.headline: L’Europe a besoin de Nvidia et il faudra plus qu’un scandale d’espionnage pour que ça change
stories.text: Jensen Huang, CEO of Nvidia, met with leaders including King Charles, Emmanuel Macron, and German Chancellor Friedrich Merz in Europe in October. Nvidia opened an internal investigation after its CEO acknowledged a relationship with a Chinese businesswoman suspected of trying to pass confidential information to Beijing. Michael McCaul, a Republican representative from Texas, posted on X that the United States should immediately suspend shipments of advanced AI chips to China. The European Union plans to acquire chips worth 40 billion euros under its trade agreement with the United States. In late July, the European Commission launched a project to build seven massive AI computing centers representing an investment of 30 billion euros. Nvidia does not manufacture its own chips but designs them and relies on companies such as TSMC in Taiwan to produce them.

stories.headline: Axis Bank wants AI to hold borrowers’ hands
stories.text: Axis Bank is developing an artificial intelligence assistant to help customers navigate online loan applications and improve conversion rates. Axis Bank group head Sameer Shetty stated that out of every 100 people starting a personal loan application, only 8 complete the process and receive disbursements. Axis Bank expects that introducing an interactive artificial intelligence guide could increase the loan completion rate to between 12% and 15%. Axis Bank's technology budget now accounts for 10% of operating expenses, an increase from 8.5% three years ago. State Bank of India plans to invest $1 billion to build a comprehensive artificial intelligence framework, according to chief information officer Abhay Pandey. Axis Bank appointed Namrata Dubashi as its artificial intelligence officer in June to lead its artificial intelligence strategies.

stories.headline: We Think That There Are More Issues For UFO Moviez India (NSE:UFO) Than Just Sluggish Earnings
stories.text: UFO Moviez India Limited released a lackluster earnings announcement last week which did not cause the stock price to sink. UFO Moviez India Limited received a profit boost of ₹40m in unusual items over the last year according to data.
